title.en: Volume 60 Biographies 25: Cui Zhongfang, Yu Zhongwen, Duan Wenzhen
title.raw: 卷60 列傳第25 崔仲方 于仲文 段文振 Volume 60 Biographies 25: Cui Zhongfang, Yu Zhongwen, Duan Wenzhen

sentences.zh: 崔仲方崔仲方，字不齊，博陵安平人也。

translations.literal: Cui Zhongfang—Cui Zhongfang, style name Buqi, was a native of Anping in Boling.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Zhongfang, whose style name was Buqi, came from Anping in Boling commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖孝芬，魏荊州刺史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Xiaofen was Governor of Jing Province in Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Cui Xiaofen had served as inspector of Jing province under the Northern Wei.

sentences.zh: 父宣猷，周小司徒。

translations.literal: His father Xuanyou was Junior Minister of Education in Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Cui Xuanyou had been junior minister of education under the Northern Zhou.

sentences.zh: 仲方少好讀書，有文武才幹。

translations.literal: Zhongfang from youth loved reading and possessed both civil and military talent.
translations.idiomatic: From boyhood Zhongfang loved books and showed talent in both civil and military affairs.

sentences.zh: 年十五，周太祖見而異之，令與諸子同就學。

translations.literal: At age fifteen, Emperor Taizu of Zhou saw him and regarded him as extraordinary, ordering him to study together with his sons.
translations.idiomatic: When he was fifteen, Emperor Wen of Zhou took notice of him and had him study alongside the imperial princes.

sentences.zh: 時高祖亦在其中，由是與高祖少相款密。

translations.literal: At that time Gaozu was also among them; from this he and Gaozu in youth were rather close and intimate.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Sui was among that group as well, and the two formed a close friendship in their youth.

sentences.zh: 後以明經為晉公宇文護參軍事，尋轉記室，遷司玉大夫，與斛斯徵、柳敏等同修禮律。

translations.literal: Later, through mastery of the Classics, he became staff officer to Duke of Jin Yuwen Hu; soon he was transferred to recorder, promoted to Grand Master of Jade, and together with Husi Zheng, Liu Min, and others revised rites and laws.
translations.idiomatic: He later entered service through the classics examination as an aide to Yuwen Hu, Duke of Jin, then became his recorder and rose to grand master of jade, joining Husi Zheng, Liu Min, and others in revising ritual and penal codes.

sentences.zh: 後以軍功，授平東將軍、銀青光祿大夫，賜爵石城縣男，邑三百戶。

translations.literal: Later, through military merit, he was appointed General Who Pacifies the East and Grand Master with Silver-Green Tally, enfeoffed as Baron of Shicheng with a fief of three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Military service later won him the posts of general who pacifies the east and grand master with silver-green tally, along with the barony of Shicheng and a fief of three hundred households.

sentences.zh: 時武帝陰有滅齊之志，仲方獻二十策，帝大奇之。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Wu secretly harbored the intent to destroy Qi; Zhongfang presented twenty stratagems, and the Emperor was greatly struck by them.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu was secretly planning the conquest of Qi, Zhongfang submitted twenty proposals that greatly impressed him.

sentences.zh: 後與少內史趙芬刪定格式。

translations.literal: Later he joined Junior Palace Secretary Zhao Fen in revising statutes and formats.
translations.idiomatic: He later worked with junior palace secretary Zhao Fen to revise administrative statutes and formats.

sentences.zh: 尋從帝攻晉州，齊之亞將崔景嵩請為內應，仲方與段文振等登城應接，遂下晉州，語在《文振傳》。

translations.literal: Soon he followed the Emperor in attacking Jinzhou; Qi's deputy general Cui Jingsong requested to act as insider, and Zhongfang with Duan Wenzhen and others ascended the wall to meet them, whereupon Jinzhou was taken—the account is in the 'Biography of Wenzhen.'
translations.idiomatic: He soon joined the emperor's assault on Jinzhou, where Qi's deputy commander Cui Jingsong offered to act as an inside contact; Zhongfang and Duan Wenzhen climbed the walls to receive him, and Jinzhou fell—as related in Duan Wenzhen's biography.

sentences.zh: 又令仲方說翼城等四城，下之。

translations.literal: He was again ordered to persuade Yicheng and four other cities, and they submitted.
translations.idiomatic: The court also sent him to win over Yicheng and three other cities, all of which surrendered.

sentences.zh: 授儀同，進爵范陽縣侯。

translations.literal: He was appointed Colonel of the First Rank and advanced in rank to Marquis of Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was made a colonel of the first rank and promoted to marquis of Fanyang county.

sentences.zh: 後以行軍長史從郯公王軌擒陳將吳明徹于呂梁，仲方計策居多。

translations.literal: Later, as campaign chief clerk he followed Duke of Tan Wang Gui in capturing Chen general Wu Mingche at Lüliang; Zhongfang's plans and stratagems predominated.
translations.idiomatic: As campaign chief clerk he later followed Prince of Tan Wang Gui in capturing the Chen general Wu Mingche at Lüliang, and most of the strategy was his.

sentences.zh: 宣帝嗣位，為少內史，奉使淮南而還。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuan succeeded to the throne, he became Junior Palace Secretary and, on a mission to Huainan, returned.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Xuan came to the throne he served as junior palace secretary and returned from a mission to Huainan.

sentences.zh: 會帝崩，高祖為丞相，與仲方相見，握手極歡，仲方亦歸心焉。

translations.literal: It happened that the Emperor died; Gaozu became Chancellor, met Zhongfang, clasped hands in extreme joy, and Zhongfang also gave his heart to him.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor died soon afterward, Yang Jian became chancellor; he and Zhongfang met and greeted each other with great warmth, and Zhongfang gave him his full loyalty.

sentences.zh: 其夜上便宜十八事，高祖並嘉納之。

translations.literal: That night he submitted eighteen timely proposals, and Gaozu praised and accepted them all.
translations.idiomatic: That same night he submitted eighteen timely proposals, all of which Yang Jian welcomed and adopted.

sentences.zh: 又見眾望有歸，陰勸高祖應天受命，高祖從之。

translations.literal: Seeing also that popular expectation was turning toward him, he secretly urged Gaozu to respond to Heaven and receive the Mandate; Gaozu followed this.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing that popular support was gathering around Yang Jian, he privately urged him to accept Heaven's mandate and take the throne, and Yang Jian followed his counsel.

sentences.zh: 及受禪，上召仲方與高熲議正朔服色事。

translations.literal: When he received the abdication, the Emperor summoned Zhongfang and Gao Jiong to discuss the calendar and ceremonial colors.
translations.idiomatic: After he took the throne, the emperor summoned Zhongfang and Gao Jiong to discuss the calendar and court ritual colors.

sentences.zh: 仲方曰：「晉為金行，後魏為水，周為木。

translations.literal: Zhongfang said: 'Jin was the Metal phase; Later Wei was Water; Zhou was Wood.'
translations.idiomatic: Zhongfang said, "Jin belonged to the phase of metal, Later Wei to water, and Zhou to wood.

sentences.zh: 皇家以火承木，得天之統。

translations.literal: Our house, taking Fire to succeed Wood, has obtained Heaven's succession.
translations.idiomatic: Our dynasty takes fire to succeed wood and thus holds Heaven's proper succession.

sentences.zh: 又聖躬載誕之初，有赤光之瑞，車服旗牲，並宜用赤。

translations.literal: Moreover, at the very beginning when the sacred person was born, there was an auspice of red light; carriages, robes, banners, and sacrificial animals should all use red.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, at Your Majesty's birth there was an omen of red light; carriages, robes, banners, and sacrificial animals should all be red.

sentences.zh: 」又勸上除六官，請依漢、魏之舊。

translations.literal: ' He also urged the Emperor to abolish the Six Offices and requested following the old systems of Han and Wei.
translations.idiomatic: " He also urged the emperor to abolish the six-office system and restore the institutions of Han and Wei.

sentences.zh: 上皆從之。

translations.literal: The Emperor followed all of this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted all of these recommendations.

sentences.zh: 進位上開府，尋轉司農少卿，進爵安固縣公。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Senior Colonel and soon transferred to Vice Minister of Agriculture, and advanced in rank to Duke of Angu.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to senior colonel, soon made vice minister of agriculture, and raised to duke of Angu county.

sentences.zh: 令發丁三萬，于朔方、靈武築長城，東至黃河，西拒綏州，南至勃出嶺，綿亙七百里。

translations.literal: He was ordered to levy thirty thousand corvée laborers to build the Long Wall at Shuofang and Lingwu, east to the Yellow River, west blocking Suizhou, south to Bochu Ridge, stretching seven hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to levy thirty thousand laborers to build the Great Wall at Shuofang and Lingwu, from the Yellow River in the east to Suizhou in the west and Bochu Ridge in the south—a stretch of seven hundred li.

sentences.zh: 明年，上複令仲方發丁十五萬，于朔方已東緣邊險要築數十城，以遏胡寇。

translations.literal: The next year, the Emperor again ordered Zhongfang to levy one hundred fifty thousand corvée laborers to build several dozen fortresses along the frontier east of Shuofang at strategic passes, to check Hu raiders.
translations.idiomatic: The following year the emperor again ordered Zhongfang to levy one hundred fifty thousand men to build several dozen fortresses along the strategic border east of Shuofang to hold back the northern raiders.

sentences.zh: 丁父艱去職。

translations.literal: Upon his father's death he left office.
translations.idiomatic: He left office to observe mourning for his father.

sentences.zh: 未期，起為虢州刺史。

translations.literal: Before the mourning period had ended, he was recalled to serve as Governor of Guo Province.
translations.idiomatic: Before his mourning term had ended he was recalled and appointed governor of Guo province.

sentences.zh: 上書論取陳之策曰：

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial discussing the strategy for taking Chen, saying:
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial on the strategy for conquering Chen, which read:

sentences.zh: 臣謹案晉太康元年歲在庚子，晉武平吳，至今開皇六年，歲次丙午，合三百七載。

translations.literal: Your servant respectfully notes that in the first year of Taikang of Jin, the year being gengzi, Jin Wu pacified Wu; from then until the present sixth year of Kaihuang, the year being bingwu, it totals three hundred seven years.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant notes that Jin's conquest of Wu in the first year of Taikang (gengzi) was three hundred seven years ago; the present sixth year of Kaihuang is the year bingwu.

sentences.zh: 《春秋寶乾圖》雲：「王者三百年一蠲法。

translations.literal: The 'Spring and Autumn Precious Qian Diagram' says: 'Every three hundred years a king remits the laws.'
translations.idiomatic: The Spring and Autumn Precious Qian Diagram says, "Every three hundred years a true king remits the laws.

sentences.zh: 」今年三百之期，可謂備矣。

translations.literal: ' This year the period of three hundred is complete and may be said to be fulfilled.
translations.idiomatic: " This year completes that three-hundred-year cycle.

sentences.zh: 陳氏草竊，起於丙子，至今丙午，又子午為沖，陰陽之忌。

translations.literal: The Chen house usurped in wild grass, rising in bingzi; until the present bingwu; moreover zi and wu are in mutual clash—the taboo of yin and yang.
translations.idiomatic: The Chen regime began its usurpation in the year bingzi and now reaches bingwu; moreover zi and wu are mutually opposed—a yin-yang omen of destruction.

sentences.zh: 昔史趙有言曰：「陳，顓頊之族，為水，故歲在鶉火以滅。

translations.literal: Formerly Shi Zhao had a saying: 'Chen is of the clan of Zhuanxu, belongs to Water, and therefore in the year of the Quail Fire constellation it perishes.'
translations.idiomatic: Shi Zhao of old said, "Chen is of the line of Zhuanxu and belongs to the element of water; it is therefore destroyed in the years of the Quail Fire asterism.

sentences.zh: 」又雲：「周武王克商，封胡公滿于陳。

translations.literal: ' It also says: 'King Wu of Zhou conquered Shang and enfeoffed Duke Hu Man in Chen.'
translations.idiomatic: " It is also said that when King Wu of Zhou conquered Shang he enfeoffed Duke Hu Man in Chen.

sentences.zh: 」至魯昭公九年，陳災，裨灶曰：「歲五及鶉火而後陳亡，楚克之。

translations.literal: ' By the ninth year of Duke Zhao of Lu, Chen suffered disaster; Pi Zao said: 'When the year reaches the fifth cycle of Quail Fire, then Chen will perish and Chu will conquer it.'
translations.idiomatic: " In the ninth year of Duke Zhao of Lu, when fire struck Chen, the astrologer Pi Zao said, "After five cycles of the Quail Fire years Chen will fall and Chu will conquer it.

sentences.zh: 」楚，祝融之後也，為火正，故覆滅陳。

translations.literal: ' Chu was descendant of Zhurong, held the office of Director of Fire, and therefore overthrew and destroyed Chen.
translations.idiomatic: " Chu was descended from Zhurong and held the office of director of fire; that is why it overthrew Chen.

sentences.zh: 陳承舜後，舜承顓頊，雖太歲左行，歲星右轉，鶉火之歲，陳族再亡，戊午之年，媯虞運盡。

translations.literal: Chen succeeded Shun's line; Shun succeeded Zhuanxu. Though the Grand Year moves left and the Year Star turns right, in years of Quail Fire the Chen clan perishes twice; in the year wuwu the fortune of Gui and Yu is exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Chen traces its line through Shun to Zhuanxu; though the Grand Year moves leftward and Jupiter rightward, in Quail Fire years the house of Chen has twice been destroyed, and in the year wuwu the fortune of the Gui and Yu lines ran out.

sentences.zh: 語跡雖殊，考事無別。

translations.literal: Though the wording and traces differ, examining the events there is no difference.
translations.idiomatic: The wording differs, but the underlying pattern is the same.

sentences.zh: 皇朝五運相承，感火德而王，國號為隋，與楚同分。

translations.literal: Our dynasty's Five Phases succeed one another; moved by the virtue of Fire it rules; the state name is Sui, sharing the same allotment as Chu.
translations.idiomatic: Our dynasty inherits the succession of the five phases, took the throne through the virtue of fire, bears the name Sui, and shares the same astrological allotment as Chu.

sentences.zh: 楚是火正，午為鶉火，未為鶉首，申為實沉，酉為大樑。

translations.literal: Chu is Director of Fire; wu is Quail Fire, wei is Quail Head, shen is Real Sink, you is Great Beam.
translations.idiomatic: Chu held the office of director of fire; the years wu, wei, shen, and you correspond to Quail Fire, Quail Head, Real Sink, and Great Beam.

sentences.zh: 既當周、秦、晉、趙之分，若當此分發兵，將得歲之助，以今量古，陳滅不疑。

translations.literal: These fall within the allotments of Zhou, Qin, Jin, and Zhao; if troops are dispatched in these allotments, they will obtain the year's assistance; measuring antiquity by the present, Chen's destruction admits no doubt.
translations.idiomatic: These years fall within the territorial allotments of Zhou, Qin, Jin, and Zhao; if we campaign in these years we shall have Jupiter's aid, and judged by past precedent Chen's fall is beyond doubt.

sentences.zh: 臣謂午未申酉，並是數極。

translations.literal: Your servant considers wu, wei, shen, and you all to be the extremity of number.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant holds that the years wu, wei, shen, and you all mark the limit of a cycle.

sentences.zh: 蓋聞天時不如地利，地利不如人和，況主聖臣良，兵強國富，動植回心，人神葉契。

translations.literal: I have heard that Heaven's seasons are inferior to Earth's advantages, and Earth's advantages inferior to human harmony; moreover, the ruler is sage and ministers good, troops strong and state rich, moving things and plants turn their hearts, men and spirits unite in accord.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's timing is less decisive than terrain, and terrain less than human unity; moreover, the ruler is sage, his ministers capable, the army strong and the treasury full, and all living things and spirits stand in accord.

sentences.zh: 陳既主昏於上，民讟於下，險無百二之固，眾非九國之師。

translations.literal: Chen already has a benighted ruler above and murmuring people below; its defenses lack the hundredfold strength of Qin's passes, and its hosts are not the armies of the nine states.
translations.idiomatic: Chen's ruler is benighted above and the people murmur below; its terrain lacks the impregnable strength of old Qin, and its forces are not the armies of the Warring States.

sentences.zh: 夏癸、殷辛尚不能立，獨此島夷而稽天討！

translations.literal: Xia Gui and Yin Xin could not even stand firm—how much less this island barbarian who delays Heaven's punishment!
translations.idiomatic: Jie of Xia and Zhou of Shang could not even hold their thrones—how can these island barbarians delay Heaven's punishment?

sentences.zh: 伏度朝廷自有宏謨，但芻蕘所見，冀申螢爝。

translations.literal: Your servant presumes the court already has great plans, but what this haycutter sees he hopes may add a glimmer to the torch.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant assumes the court already has a grand strategy; these humble observations are offered only in hope of adding a little light.

sentences.zh: 今唯須武昌已下，蘄、和、滁、方、吳、海等州更帖精兵，密營渡計。

translations.literal: Now one need only from Wuchang downstream post elite troops at Qi, He, Chu, Fang, Wu, Hai, and other prefectures and secretly prepare crossing plans.
translations.idiomatic: For the present, from Wuchang downstream the prefectures of Qi, He, Chu, Fang, Wu, Hai, and others should be reinforced with elite troops while crossing plans are prepared in secret.

sentences.zh: 益、信、襄、荊、基、郢等州速造舟楫，多張形勢，為水戰之具。

translations.literal: Yi, Xin, Xiang, Jing, Ji, Ying, and other prefectures should quickly build boats and oars, display many formations, and prepare equipment for river battle.
translations.idiomatic: The prefectures of Yi, Xin, Xiang, Jing, Ji, Ying, and others should quickly build fleets, display large forces, and prepare for naval warfare.

sentences.zh: 蜀、漢二江，是其上流，水路衝要，必爭之所。

translations.literal: The two rivers Shu and Han are its upper reaches; the water route is strategically critical and a place both sides must contest.
translations.idiomatic: The Shu and Han rivers form the upper Yangtze—its key water route and the ground both sides must fight for.

sentences.zh: 賊雖于流頭、荊門、延州、公安、巴陵、隱磯、夏首、蘄口、盆城置船，然終聚漢口、峽口，以水戰大決。

translations.literal: Though the enemy stations ships at Liutou, Jingmen, Yanzhou, Gong'an, Baling, Yinji, Xiashou, Qikou, and Pencheng, in the end they will gather at Hankou and Xiakou for the great decision by water battle.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy may station ships at Liutou, Jingmen, Yanzhou, Gong'an, Baling, Yinji, Xiashou, Qikou, and Pencheng, but in the end they will mass at Hankou and the gorge for the decisive naval battle.

sentences.zh: 若賊必以上流有軍，令精兵赴援者，下流諸將即須擇便橫渡。

translations.literal: If the enemy is certain there are troops upstream and sends elite forces to reinforce, the generals downstream must at once choose a favorable point to cross over.
translations.idiomatic: If the enemy, finding troops upstream, sends elite forces to reinforce, our downstream commanders must seize a favorable moment to cross the river.

sentences.zh: 如擁眾自衛，上江水軍鼓行以前。

translations.literal: If they merely mass troops for self-defense, the upstream river army should advance with drums beating.
translations.idiomatic: If they merely mass troops for self-defense, the upstream fleet should advance with drums beating.

sentences.zh: 雖恃九江五湖之險，非德無以為固，徒有三吳、百越之兵，無恩不能自立。

translations.literal: Though they rely on the dangers of the Nine Rivers and Five Lakes, without virtue they have nothing wherewith to make firm; they merely have the troops of Three Wu and Hundred Yue—without grace they cannot stand on their own.
translations.idiomatic: Though they rely on the defenses of the Yangtze lakes, without virtue they cannot hold firm; though they have the armies of Wu and Yue, without benevolence they cannot stand alone.

sentences.zh: 上覽而大悅，轉基州刺史，征入朝。

translations.literal: The Emperor read it and was greatly pleased, transferred him to Governor of Ji Province, and summoned him to court.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor read the memorial with great delight, transferred him to governor of Ji province, and summoned him to court.

sentences.zh: 仲方因面陳經略，上善之，賜以禦袍袴，並雜彩五百段，進位開府而遣之。

translations.literal: Zhongfang thereupon presented his strategy in person; the Emperor approved it, bestowed imperial robes and trousers plus five hundred lengths of assorted silks, advanced him to Colonelate, and sent him off.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongfang then presented his strategy in person; the emperor approved it, granted him imperial robes and trousers plus five hundred lengths of colored silk, promoted him to colonelate, and sent him on his way.

sentences.zh: 及大舉伐陳，以仲方為行軍總管，率兵與秦王會。

translations.literal: When a great campaign was launched against Chen, Zhongfang was made campaign commander-in-chief, leading troops to join the Prince of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: When the great campaign against Chen was launched, he was made campaign commander-in-chief and led his forces to join Prince Qin.

sentences.zh: 及陳平，坐事免。

translations.literal: When Chen was pacified, he was dismissed from office for an offense.
translations.idiomatic: After Chen was conquered he was dismissed for an offense.

sentences.zh: 未幾，復位。

translations.literal: Before long he was restored to office.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was restored to office.

sentences.zh: 後數載，轉會州總管。

translations.literal: Several years later he was transferred to Commander-in-Chief of Huizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later he was made commander-in-chief of Huizhou.

sentences.zh: 時諸羌猶未賓附，詔令仲方擊之，與賊三十餘戰，紫祖、四鄰、望方、涉題、幹碉、小鐵圍山、白男王、弱水等諸部悉平。

translations.literal: At that time the various Qiang had not yet submitted; an edict ordered Zhongfang to attack them. He fought the enemy more than thirty battles and pacified the tribes Zizu, Silin, Wangfang, Sheti, Ganbao, Little Iron Enclosure Mountain, White Male King, Ruoshui, and others entirely.
translations.idiomatic: The Qiang tribes had not yet submitted; the court ordered Zhongfang to attack them. After more than thirty battles he pacified the Zizu, Silin, Wangfang, Sheti, Ganbao, Little Iron Enclosure Mountain, White Male King, Ruoshui, and other groups.

sentences.zh: 賜奴婢一百三十口，黃金三十斤，雜物稱是。

translations.literal: He was granted one hundred thirty male and female servants, thirty jin of gold, and miscellaneous goods in proportion.
translations.idiomatic: He was rewarded with one hundred thirty servants, thirty jin of gold, and a comparable quantity of other goods.

sentences.zh: 仁壽初，授代州總管，在職數年，被征入朝。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Renshou he was appointed Commander-in-Chief of Daizhou; after several years in office he was summoned to court.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Renshou era he was made commander-in-chief of Daizhou; after several years he was recalled to court.

sentences.zh: 會上崩，漢王諒餘党據呂州不下，煬帝令周羅睺攻之，中流矢卒，乃令仲方代總其眾，月餘拔之。

translations.literal: It happened that the Emperor died; remnant factions of Prince of Han Yang Liang held Luzhou and would not submit. Emperor Yang ordered Zhou Luohou to attack it; struck by a stray arrow he died, whereupon Zhongfang was ordered to take command of his troops; in a little over a month it was taken.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor died, remnants of Prince Liang of Han held Luzhou. Emperor Yang ordered Zhou Luohou to attack it, but Zhou was killed by a stray arrow; Zhongfang was then put in command of his forces and took the city in little more than a month.

sentences.zh: 進位大將軍，拜民部尚書，尋轉禮部尚書。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Great General and appointed Minister of the Household; soon he was transferred to Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to great general and appointed minister of the household, then soon made minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 後三載，坐事免。

translations.literal: Three years later he was dismissed for an offense.
translations.idiomatic: Three years later he was dismissed for an offense.

sentences.zh: 尋為國子祭酒，轉太常卿。

translations.literal: Soon he became Libationer of the Imperial Academy and was transferred to Minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made libationer of the imperial academy and then minister of ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以其衰老，出拜上郡太守。

translations.literal: The court, considering him aged, sent him out as Governor of Shang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Because of his age the court sent him out as governor of Shang commandery.

sentences.zh: 未幾，以母憂去職。

translations.literal: Before long he left office on account of his mother's death.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he left office to mourn his mother.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，起為信都太守，上表乞骸骨，優詔許之。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was recalled to serve as Governor of Xindu; he submitted a memorial requesting to retire, and a gracious edict permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: After a year he was recalled as governor of Xindu, submitted a memorial asking to retire, and received a gracious edict granting his request.

sentences.zh: 尋卒于家，時年七十六。

translations.literal: Soon he died at home, aged seventy-six.
translations.idiomatic: He soon died at home at the age of seventy-six.

sentences.zh: 子民壽，官至定陶令。

translations.literal: His son Minshou reached the office of Magistrate of Dingtao.
translations.idiomatic: His son Minshou rose to the post of magistrate of Dingtao.

sentences.zh: 于仲文于仲文，字次武，建平公義之兄子。

translations.literal: Yu Zhongwen—Yu Zhongwen, style name Ciwu, was the elder brother's son of Duke of Jianping Yu Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Zhongwen, whose style name was Ciwu, was a nephew of Duke Jianping Yu Yi.

sentences.zh: 父寔，周大左輔、燕國公。

translations.literal: His father Shi was Grand Left Assistant and Duke of Yan in Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yu Shi had been grand left assistant and duke of Yan under the Northern Zhou.

sentences.zh: 仲文少聰敏，髫齔就學，耽閱不倦。

translations.literal: Zhongwen from youth was clever and keen; in childhood he began study and was absorbed in reading without weariness.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongwen was clever from childhood; he began his studies early and read with tireless devotion.

sentences.zh: 其父異之曰：「此兒必興吾宗矣。

translations.literal: His father regarded him as extraordinary and said: 'This boy will surely revive our clan.'
translations.idiomatic: His father marveled at him and said, "This boy will surely bring glory to our house.

sentences.zh: 」九歲，嘗于雲陽宮見周太祖，太祖問曰：「聞兒好讀書，書有何事？

translations.literal: ' At age nine he once saw Emperor Taizu of Zhou at Yunyang Palace; Taizu asked: 'I hear the boy loves reading—what is reading about?'
translations.idiomatic: " When he was nine he once met Emperor Wen of Zhou at Yunyang Palace. The emperor asked, "I hear you love books—what are books about?

sentences.zh: 」仲文對曰：「資父事君，忠孝而已。

translations.literal: ' Zhongwen replied: 'To support one's father and serve one's lord—loyalty and filial piety, that is all.'
translations.idiomatic: " Zhongwen answered, "To support one's father and serve one's lord—loyalty and filial piety, nothing more.

sentences.zh: 」太祖甚嗟歎之。

translations.literal: ' Taizu greatly sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor sighed in deep admiration.

sentences.zh: 其後就博士李祥受《周易》、《三禮》。

translations.literal: Afterward he studied under Erudite Li Xiang the 'Book of Changes' and the 'Three Rites.'
translations.idiomatic: He later studied the Book of Changes and the Three Rites under the erudite Li Xiang.

sentences.zh: 略通大義。

translations.literal: He gained a general grasp of their great principles.
translations.idiomatic: He gained a general grasp of their essential meaning.

sentences.zh: 及長，倜儻有大志，氣調英拔，當時號為名公子。

translations.literal: When grown, he was free-spirited with great ambition, his bearing lofty and outstanding, and of the time was styled a famous young noble.
translations.idiomatic: As a young man he was bold and ambitious, with a striking presence, and was known as a leading gentleman of his day.

sentences.zh: 起家為趙王屬，尋遷安固太守。

translations.literal: He began his career as aide to the Prince of Zhao and soon was transferred to Governor of Angu.
translations.idiomatic: He began his career as an aide to the Prince of Zhao and was soon made governor of Angu.

sentences.zh: 有任、杜兩家各失牛，後得一牛，兩家俱認，州郡久不能決。

translations.literal: The Ren and Du families each lost an ox; later one ox was found and both families claimed it; the province and commandery long could not decide.
translations.idiomatic: The Ren and Du families each lost an ox; when one ox was later found, both claimed it, and the provincial authorities could not settle the dispute for a long time.

sentences.zh: 益州長史韓伯俊曰：「于安固少聰察，可令決之。

translations.literal: Chief Clerk of Yizhou Han Bojun said: 'Young Lord Angu is keen and perceptive—he may be ordered to decide it.'
translations.idiomatic: The chief clerk of Yizhou, Han Bojun, said, "The young governor of Angu is sharp-witted; let him decide the case.

sentences.zh: 」仲文對曰：「此易解耳。

translations.literal: ' Zhongwen replied: 'This is easy to resolve.'
translations.idiomatic: " Zhongwen replied, "That is easily settled.

sentences.zh: 」於是令二家各驅牛群至，乃放所認者，遂向任氏群中。

translations.literal: ' Thereupon he ordered both families each to drive their herds of oxen forward, then released the ox in dispute, and it went straight toward the Ren family's herd.
translations.idiomatic: " He had both families drive their herds forward, then released the disputed ox, which went straight to the Ren family's herd.

sentences.zh: 又陰使人微傷其牛，任氏嗟惋，杜家自若。

translations.literal: He also secretly had someone slightly injure the ox; the Ren family sighed in distress, while the Du family remained composed.
translations.idiomatic: He then secretly had the ox slightly injured; the Ren family lamented while the Du family remained unmoved.

sentences.zh: 仲文於是訶詰杜氏，杜氏服罪而去。

translations.literal: Zhongwen thereupon rebuked and questioned the Du family; the Du family confessed guilt and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongwen then interrogated the Du family, who confessed and withdrew their claim.

sentences.zh: 始州刺史屈突尚，宇文護之黨也，先坐事下獄，無敢繩者。

translations.literal: Governor of Shizhou Qutu Shang was a partisan of Yuwen Hu; he had earlier been imprisoned for an offense, and no one dared to prosecute him.
translations.idiomatic: Qutu Shang, governor of Shizhou, was a partisan of Yuwen Hu who had earlier been imprisoned for crimes, yet no one dared prosecute him further.

sentences.zh: 仲文至郡窮治，遂竟其獄。

translations.literal: When Zhongwen arrived in the commandery he pursued the case to the end and completed the trial.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhongwen took office he pursued the case to the end and brought it to judgment.

sentences.zh: 蜀中為之語曰：「明斷無雙有于公，不避強禦有次武。

translations.literal: Shu coined a saying about him: 'In clear judgment without peer there is Lord Yu; in not shunning the powerful there is Ciwu.'
translations.idiomatic: Shu coined a saying about him: "For matchless judgment there is Lord Yu; for fearlessness before the powerful there is Ciwu.

sentences.zh: 」未幾，征為禦正下大夫，封延壽郡公，邑三千五百戶。

translations.literal: ' Before long he was summoned as Junior Master of Correctness and enfeoffed as Duke of Yanshou with a fief of three thousand five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: " Before long he was summoned to court as junior master of correctness and enfeoffed as duke of Yanshou with a fief of three thousand five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 數從征伐，累勳授儀同三司。

translations.literal: He repeatedly followed campaigns; through accumulated merit he was appointed Colonel of the Third Rank.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in many campaigns and, through accumulated merit, was made colonel of the third rank.

sentences.zh: 宣帝時，為東郡太守。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Xuan he was Governor of Dong Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xuan he served as governor of Dong commandery.

sentences.zh: 高祖為丞相，尉迥作亂，遣將檀讓收河南之地。

translations.literal: When Gaozu was Chancellor, Yu Chi rebelled and sent the general Tan Rang to seize the lands of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Jian was chancellor, Yu Chi rebelled and sent the general Tan Rang to seize Henan.

sentences.zh: 復使人誘致仲文，仲文拒之。

translations.literal: He again sent men to entice Zhongwen to join him; Zhongwen refused.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent envoys to win Zhongwen over, but Zhongwen refused.

sentences.zh: 迥怒其不同己，遣儀同宇文威攻之。

translations.literal: Chi was angry that he would not side with him and sent Colonel Yuwen Wei to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Chi, angered by his refusal, sent the colonel Yuwen Wei to attack him.

sentences.zh: 仲文迎擊，大破威眾，斬首五百餘級。

translations.literal: Zhongwen met the attack and greatly defeated Wei's forces, taking more than five hundred heads.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongwen met the attack and routed Wei's army, taking more than five hundred heads.

sentences.zh: 以功授開府。

translations.literal: For his merit he was appointed Grand Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: For this achievement he was granted the rank of Grand Guardian.

sentences.zh: 迥又遣其將宇文胄渡石濟，宇文威、鄒紹自白馬，二道俱進，復攻仲文。

translations.literal: Chi again sent his general Yuwen Zhou to cross the Shiji ford, and Yuwen Wei and Zou Shao from Baima; both routes advanced together and again attacked Zhongwen.
translations.idiomatic: Chi then sent his general Yuwen Zhou across the Shiji crossing while Yuwen Wei and Zou Shao marched from Baima; the two columns advanced together and again attacked Zhongwen.

sentences.zh: 賊勢逾盛，人情大駭，郡人赫連僧伽、敬子哲率眾應迥。

translations.literal: The rebels' momentum grew ever stronger; popular sentiment was greatly terrified; commandery men Helian Sengqie and Jing Zizi led the multitude to respond to Chi.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel strength mounted and terror spread among the people; Helian Sengqie and Jing Zizi of the commandery rallied crowds to join Chi.

sentences.zh: 仲文自度不能支，棄妻子，將六十餘騎，開城西門，潰圍而遁。

translations.literal: Zhongwen reckoned he could not hold out; abandoning his wife and children, he took a little more than sixty horsemen, opened the west gate of the city, broke through the encirclement, and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Judging that he could not hold the city, Zhongwen abandoned his wife and children, took a little more than sixty horsemen, opened the west gate, broke through the siege, and escaped.

sentences.zh: 為賊所追，且戰且行，所從騎戰死者十七八。

translations.literal: Pursued by the rebels, he fought as he went; of the horsemen who followed him, seven or eight in ten died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Pursued by the enemy, he fought as he withdrew; seven or eight of every ten horsemen with him fell in battle.

sentences.zh: 仲文僅而獲免，達于京師。

translations.literal: Zhongwen barely escaped with his life and reached the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongwen barely escaped with his life and reached the capital.

sentences.zh: 迥於是屠其三子一女。

translations.literal: Chi thereupon slaughtered his three sons and one daughter.
translations.idiomatic: Chi then put his three sons and one daughter to the sword.

sentences.zh: 高祖見之，引入臥內，為之下泣。

translations.literal: When Gaozu saw him, he brought him into his private chamber and wept for him.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu received him, he brought him into his private chamber and wept for him.

sentences.zh: 賜綵五百段，黃金二百兩，進位大將軍，領河南道行軍總管。

translations.literal: He was granted five hundred bolts of colored silk and two hundred taels of gold, promoted to Grand General, and appointed Commander-in-Chief of the Henan Circuit campaign.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted five hundred bolts of colored silk and two hundred taels of gold, promoted to grand general, and made commander-in-chief of the Henan circuit campaign.

sentences.zh: 給以鼓吹，馳傳詣洛陽發兵，以討檀讓。

translations.literal: He was given a guard of musicians, sent by post relay to Luoyang to raise troops, and ordered to attack Tan Rang.
translations.idiomatic: He was given a guard of musicians and sent by post relay to Luoyang to raise troops and attack Tan Rang.

sentences.zh: 時韋孝寬拒迥於永橋，仲文詣孝寬有所計議。

translations.literal: At that time Wei Xiaokuan was holding Chi at Yong Bridge; Zhongwen went to Xiaokuan to discuss plans.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Wei Xiaokuan was holding Chi at Yong Bridge, and Zhongwen went to consult with him.

sentences.zh: 時總管宇文忻頗有自疑之心，因謂仲文曰：「公新從京師來，觀執政意何如也？

translations.literal: At that time the commander Yuwen Xin was much given to self-doubt, and therefore said to Zhongwen: 'You have just come from the capital—what do you make of the intentions of those in power?
translations.idiomatic: The commander Yuwen Xin was then much troubled by self-doubt and asked Zhongwen, "You have just come from the capital—what do you make of the intentions of those in power?

sentences.zh: 尉迥誠不足平，正恐事寧之後，更有藏弓之慮。

translations.literal: Yu Chi is truly not hard to suppress, but I fear that once affairs are settled there will be further worry about the bow being hidden once the birds are gone.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Chi is not hard to defeat, but I fear that once the rebellion is put down we may yet face the fate of the bow cast aside when the birds are gone.

sentences.zh: 」仲文懼忻生變，因謂之曰：「丞相寬仁大度，明識有餘，苟能竭誠，必心無貳。

translations.literal: ' Zhongwen feared that Xin might turn disloyal, and therefore said to him: 'The Chancellor is generous, humane, and broad-minded, with more than enough clear insight; if one can serve him with full sincerity, his heart will surely harbor no divided loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: " Fearing that Xin might turn disloyal, Zhongwen said to him, "The chancellor is generous, humane, and broad-minded, with more than enough clear insight; if one serves him with full sincerity, his heart will harbor no divided loyalty.

sentences.zh: 仲文在京三日，頻見三善，以此為觀，非尋常人也。

translations.literal: During Zhongwen's three days in the capital I repeatedly witnessed three acts of goodness; judged by this, he is no ordinary man.
translations.idiomatic: In my three days at the capital I repeatedly witnessed three acts of goodness; judged by that, he is no ordinary man.

sentences.zh: 」忻曰：「三善如何？

translations.literal: ' Xin said: 'What are the three acts of goodness?
translations.idiomatic: " Xin asked, "What are the three acts of goodness?

sentences.zh: 」仲文曰：「有陳萬敵者，新從賊中來，即令其弟難敵召募鄉曲，從軍討賊。

translations.literal: ' Zhongwen said: 'There was a Chen Wandi who had just come from among the rebels; the Chancellor immediately had his younger brother Nandi recruit local men and join the army to suppress the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhongwen said, "There was a Chen Wandi who had just come over from the rebels; the chancellor immediately had his younger brother Nandi recruit local men to join the army and suppress the rebels.

sentences.zh: 此其有大度一也。

translations.literal: This was his first great magnanimity.
translations.idiomatic: That was his first great magnanimity.

sentences.zh: 上士宋謙，奉使勾檢，謙緣此別求他罪。

translations.literal: Senior Clerk Song Qian, on a mission to audit and investigate, used this occasion to seek out other crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Senior clerk Song Qian, sent on an audit, used the occasion to hunt for other offenses.

sentences.zh: 丞相責之曰：'入網者自可推求，何須別訪，以虧大體。

translations.literal: The Chancellor rebuked him, saying: 'Those caught in the net can be pursued in the usual way—why must you inquire elsewhere and impair the larger principle?
translations.idiomatic: The chancellor rebuked him, saying, "Those already caught in the net can be pursued in the usual way—why must you go hunting for other offenses and impair the larger principle?

sentences.zh: '此其不求人私二也。

translations.literal: ' This was his second refusal to seek men's private faults.
translations.idiomatic: " That was his second refusal to pry into men's private faults.

sentences.zh: 言及仲文妻子，未嘗不潸泫。

translations.literal: Whenever he spoke of Zhongwen's wife and children, he never failed to shed tears.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he spoke of Zhongwen's wife and children, he never failed to shed tears.

sentences.zh: 此其有仁心三也。

translations.literal: This was his third humane heart.
translations.idiomatic: That was his third humane heart.

sentences.zh: 」忻自此遂安。

translations.literal: ' From this Xin was thereafter at ease.
translations.idiomatic: " From that point Xin was reassured.

sentences.zh: 仲文軍至汴州之東倪塢，與迥將劉子昂、劉浴德等相遇，進擊破之。

translations.literal: Zhongwen's army reached Dongni Wu east of Bian Province, encountered Chi's generals Liu Zi'ang, Liu Yude, and others, advanced to attack, and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongwen's army reached Dongni Wu east of Bian Province, met Chi's generals Liu Zi'ang, Liu Yude, and others, attacked, and defeated them.

sentences.zh: 軍次蓼堤，去梁郡七裡，讓擁眾數萬，仲文以羸師挑戰。

translations.literal: The army halted at Liaodi, seven li from Liang Commandery; Rang commanded a host of several tens of thousands, and Zhongwen challenged him with a weakened force.
translations.idiomatic: The army halted at Liaodi, seven li from Liang commandery; Rang commanded a host of several tens of thousands, and Zhongwen challenged him with a weakened force.

sentences.zh: 讓悉眾來拒，仲文偽北，讓軍頗驕。

translations.literal: Rang brought out his entire army to resist; Zhongwen feigned retreat, and Rang's army grew quite arrogant.
translations.idiomatic: Rang brought out his entire army to resist; Zhongwen feigned retreat, and Rang's army grew overconfident.

sentences.zh: 於是遣精兵左右翼擊之，大敗讓軍，生獲五千餘人，斬首七百級。

translations.literal: Thereupon he sent elite troops to strike them on left and right flanks, greatly defeated Rang's army, captured alive more than five thousand men, and took seven hundred heads.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent elite troops to strike both flanks, routed Rang's army, captured more than five thousand men alive, and took seven hundred heads.

sentences.zh: 進攻梁郡，迥守將劉子寬棄城遁走。

translations.literal: He advanced to attack Liang Commandery; Chi's defending general Liu Zikuan abandoned the city and fled.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced on Liang commandery; Chi's defending general Liu Zikuan abandoned the city and fled.

sentences.zh: 仲文追擊，擒斬數千人，子寬僅以身免。

translations.literal: Zhongwen pursued and attacked, capturing and killing several thousand men; Zikuan barely escaped with his life.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongwen pursued, capturing and killing several thousand men; Zikuan barely escaped with his life.

sentences.zh: 初，仲文在蓼堤，諸將皆曰：「軍自遠來，士馬疲敝，不可決勝。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Zhongwen was at Liaodi, all the generals said: 'The army has come from afar; men and horses are weary and worn—victory cannot be decided.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier at Liaodi, all the generals said, "The army has come from afar; men and horses are weary and worn—we cannot fight for a decisive victory.

sentences.zh: 」仲文令三軍趣食，列陣大戰。

translations.literal: ' Zhongwen ordered the three armies to take their meal and then formed ranks for a great battle.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhongwen ordered the three armies to take their meal, then formed ranks for a great battle.

sentences.zh: 既而破賊，諸將皆請曰：「前兵疲不可交戰，竟而克勝，其計安在？

translations.literal: After the rebels were defeated, all the generals asked: 'Before, the troops were weary and could not engage in battle, yet in the end you won—what was your plan?
translations.idiomatic: After the rebels were defeated, the generals all asked, "The troops were weary and unfit for battle, yet in the end you won—what was your plan?

sentences.zh: 」仲文笑曰：「吾所部將士皆山東人，果於速進，不宜持久。

translations.literal: ' Zhongwen smiled and said: 'The officers and soldiers under my command are all men of Shandong; they are bold in rapid advance and are not suited to prolonged fighting.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhongwen smiled and said, "The officers and soldiers under my command are all men of Shandong; they are bold in rapid advance and are not suited to prolonged fighting.

sentences.zh: 乘勢擊之，所以制勝。

translations.literal: Striking them while the momentum was favorable—this is how victory was secured.
translations.idiomatic: Striking while the momentum was with us—that is how victory was secured.

sentences.zh: 」諸將皆以為非所及也。

translations.literal: ' All the generals agreed that this was beyond their reach.
translations.idiomatic: " The generals all agreed that this was beyond their reach.

sentences.zh: 進擊曹州，獲迥所署刺史李仲康及上儀同房勁。

translations.literal: He advanced to attack Cao Province, capturing Chi's appointed governor Li Zhongkang and Senior Colonel Fang Jin.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced on Cao province, capturing Chi's appointed governor Li Zhongkang and senior colonel Fang Jin.

sentences.zh: 檀讓以餘眾屯城武，別將高士儒以萬人屯永昌。

translations.literal: Tan Rang encamped at Chengwu with the remnant host, while another general Gao Shiru encamped at Yongchang with ten thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Tan Rang encamped at Chengwu with the remnant force, while another general, Gao Shiru, encamped at Yongchang with ten thousand men.

sentences.zh: 仲文詐移書州縣曰：「大將軍至，可多積粟。

translations.literal: Zhongwen falsely sent dispatches to the prefectures and counties saying: 'The Grand General has arrived; you may store up much grain.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongwen sent forged dispatches to the prefectures and counties saying, "The grand general has arrived; store up extra grain.

sentences.zh: 」讓謂仲文未能卒至，方槌牛享士。

translations.literal: ' Rang thought Zhongwen could not arrive so quickly and was just beating oxen to feast his troops.
translations.idiomatic: " Rang thought Zhongwen could not arrive so soon and was just slaughtering oxen to feast his troops.

sentences.zh: 仲文知其怠，選精騎襲之，一日便至，遂拔城武。

translations.literal: Zhongwen, knowing they were slack, selected elite cavalry to strike them; in a single day he arrived, and thereupon captured Chengwu.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing they were slack, Zhongwen selected elite cavalry to strike; he arrived in a single day and captured Chengwu.

sentences.zh: 迥將席毗羅，眾十萬，屯於沛縣，將攻徐州。

translations.literal: Chi's general Xi Piluo, with a host of one hundred thousand, encamped at Pei County and was about to attack Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chi's general Xi Piluo, with a host of one hundred thousand, encamped at Pei County and was about to attack Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 其妻子在金鄉。

translations.literal: His wife and children were at Jinxiang.
translations.idiomatic: His wife and children were at Jinxiang.

sentences.zh: 仲文遣人詐為毗羅使者，謂金鄉城主徐善淨曰：「檀讓明日午時到金鄉，將宣蜀公令，賞賜將士。

translations.literal: Zhongwen sent men falsely posing as Piluo's envoys to say to Jinxiang's magistrate Xu Shanjing: 'Tan Rang will reach Jinxiang tomorrow at noon to proclaim the Duke of Shu's orders and reward the officers and soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongwen sent men disguised as Piluo's envoys to tell Jinxiang's magistrate Xu Shanjing, "Tan Rang will reach Jinxiang tomorrow at noon to proclaim the Duke of Shu's orders and reward the officers and soldiers.

sentences.zh: 」金鄉人謂為信然，皆喜。

translations.literal: ' The people of Jinxiang believed this to be true and all rejoiced.
translations.idiomatic: " The people of Jinxiang believed it and rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 仲文簡精兵，偽建迥旗幟，倍道而進。

translations.literal: Zhongwen picked elite troops, falsely raised Chi's banners and flags, and advanced at double speed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongwen picked elite troops, raised Chi's banners and flags as a ruse, and advanced at double speed.

sentences.zh: 善淨望見仲文軍且至，以為檀讓，乃出迎謁。

translations.literal: Shanjing saw Zhongwen's army about to arrive and, thinking it was Tan Rang, went out to welcome and pay his respects.
translations.idiomatic: Shanjing saw Zhongwen's army approaching, took it for Tan Rang's, and went out to welcome him.

sentences.zh: 仲文執之，遂取金鄉。

translations.literal: Zhongwen seized him and thereupon took Jinxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongwen seized him and took Jinxiang.

sentences.zh: 諸將多勸屠之，仲文曰：「此城是毗羅起兵之所，當寬其妻子，其兵可自歸。

translations.literal: Many of the generals urged that the city be slaughtered; Zhongwen said: 'This city is where Piluo raised his army; we should spare his wife and children, and his troops will surrender of themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Many generals urged a massacre; Zhongwen said, "This city is where Piluo raised his army; if we spare his wife and children, his troops will surrender of themselves.

sentences.zh: 如即屠之，彼望絕矣。

translations.literal: If we slaughter them at once, their hope will be cut off.
translations.idiomatic: If we slaughter them at once, all hope will be cut off for them.

sentences.zh: 」眾皆稱善。

translations.literal: ' All praised the plan as good.
translations.idiomatic: " All praised the plan.

sentences.zh: 於是毗羅恃眾來薄官軍，仲文背城結陣，去軍數裡，設伏于麻田中。

translations.literal: Thereupon Piluo, relying on his numbers, came to press close upon the government army; Zhongwen formed ranks with his back to the city, and several li from the army set an ambush in a hemp field.
translations.idiomatic: Piluo then relied on his numbers and pressed the government army; Zhongwen formed ranks with his back to the city and, several li from the army, set an ambush in a hemp field.

sentences.zh: 兩陣才合，伏兵發，俱曳柴鼓噪，塵埃張天。

translations.literal: As soon as the two battle lines joined, the ambush troops sprang forth; all dragged branches and beat drums and shouted, and dust filled the sky.
translations.idiomatic: As soon as the two lines joined battle, the ambush sprang forth; men dragged branches, beat drums, and shouted until dust filled the sky.

sentences.zh: 毗羅軍大潰，仲文乘之，賊皆投洙水而死，為之不流。

translations.literal: Piluo's army was greatly routed; Zhongwen pressed the pursuit, and the rebels all threw themselves into the Zhu River and drowned, so that the river ceased to flow.
translations.idiomatic: Piluo's army was routed; Zhongwen pressed the pursuit, and the rebels threw themselves into the Zhu River and drowned until the river ceased to flow.

sentences.zh: 獲檀讓，檻送京師，河南悉平。

translations.literal: Tan Rang was captured and sent to the capital in a cage; all of Henan was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Tan Rang was captured and sent to the capital in a cage; all of Henan was pacified.

sentences.zh: 毗羅匿滎陽人家，執斬之，傳首闕下。

translations.literal: Piluo hid in a household at Xingyang; he was seized and beheaded, and his head was sent to the palace gates.
translations.idiomatic: Piluo hid in a household at Xingyang; he was seized and beheaded, and his head was sent to the palace gates.

sentences.zh: 勒石紀功，樹於泗上。

translations.literal: A stone was carved to record his merit and erected on the Si River.
translations.idiomatic: A stone was carved to record his merit and erected on the Si River.

sentences.zh: 入朝京師，高祖引入臥內，宴享極歡。

translations.literal: He entered the capital to attend court; Gaozu brought him into his private chamber and feasted with him in the utmost joy.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the capital to attend court; Gaozu brought him into his private chamber and feasted with him in the utmost joy.

sentences.zh: 賜雜綵千餘段，妓女十人，拜柱國、河南道大行台。

translations.literal: He was granted more than a thousand bolts of mixed colored silk and ten singing girls, and appointed Duke of the Realm and Grand Expeditionary Commissioner of the Henan Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted more than a thousand bolts of mixed colored silk and ten singing girls, and appointed duke of the realm and grand expeditionary commissioner of the Henan circuit.

sentences.zh: 屬高祖受禪，不行。

translations.literal: Just then Gaozu accepted the abdication, and he did not take up the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Just then Gaozu accepted the abdication, and he did not take up the appointment.

sentences.zh: 未幾，其叔父太尉翼坐事下獄，仲文亦為吏所簿，於獄中上書曰：

translations.literal: Before long his uncle the Grand Marshal Yi was imprisoned for an offense, and Zhongwen was also investigated by the officials; from prison he submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: Before long his uncle, Grand Marshal Yi, was imprisoned for an offense, and Zhongwen was also investigated by the officials; from prison he submitted a memorial saying:

sentences.zh: 臣聞春生夏長，天地平分之功，子孝臣誠，人倫不易之道。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that spring begets and summer grows—the merit by which Heaven and Earth divide the year; filial sons and loyal ministers—the unchanging way of human relations.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant has heard that spring begets and summer grows—the merit by which Heaven and Earth divide the year; filial sons and loyal ministers—the unchanging way of human relations.

sentences.zh: 曩者尉迥逆亂，所在影從。

translations.literal: Formerly Yu Chi rebelled in disorder, and everywhere men followed him like shadows.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Yu Chi rebelled, and everywhere men followed him like shadows.

sentences.zh: 臣任處關河，地居衝要，嘗膽枕戈，誓以必死。

translations.literal: Your servant's post lay at the passes and rivers in a place of strategic importance; I tasted gall and slept upon my spear, vowing to die if need be.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant held a post at the passes and rivers in a place of strategic importance; I tasted gall and slept upon my spear, vowing to die if need be.

sentences.zh: 迥時購臣位大將軍、邑萬戶。

translations.literal: At that time Chi offered to buy your servant with the rank of Grand General and a fief of ten thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Chi offered to buy your servant with the rank of grand general and a fief of ten thousand households.

sentences.zh: 臣不顧妻子，不愛身命，冒白刃，潰重圍，三男一女，相繼淪沒，披露肝膽，馳赴闕庭。

translations.literal: Your servant did not regard wife and children, did not cherish life, braved naked blades, broke through heavy encirclement; three sons and one daughter perished in succession; laying bare liver and gall, I galloped to the imperial court.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant did not regard wife and children or cherish life, braved naked blades, broke through heavy encirclement; three sons and one daughter perished in succession; laying bare my loyalty, I galloped to the imperial court.

sentences.zh: 蒙陛下授臣以高官，委臣以兵革。

translations.literal: I received from Your Majesty high office and was entrusted with arms and armor.
translations.idiomatic: I received from Your Majesty high office and was entrusted with arms and armor.

sentences.zh: 于時河南凶寇，狼顧鴟張，臣以羸兵八千，掃除氛䘲。

translations.literal: At that time the fierce bandits of Henan glared back like wolves and spread like owls; your servant with eight thousand weary soldiers swept away the evil miasma.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the fierce bandits of Henan glared back like wolves and spread like owls; your servant, with eight thousand weary soldiers, swept away the evil miasma.

sentences.zh: 摧劉寬于梁郡，破檀讓於蓼堤，平曹州，復東郡、安城、武定、永昌，解亳州圍，殄徐州賊。

translations.literal: I crushed Liu Kuan at Liang Commandery, broke Tan Rang at Liaodi, pacified Cao Province, recovered Dong Commandery, Ancheng, Wuding, and Yongchang, lifted the siege of Bozhou, and exterminated the rebels of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: I crushed Liu Kuan at Liang commandery, broke Tan Rang at Liaodi, pacified Cao province, recovered Dong commandery, Ancheng, Wuding, and Yongchang, lifted the siege of Bozhou, and exterminated the rebels of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 席毗十萬之眾，一戰土崩，河南蟻聚之徒，應時戡定。

translations.literal: Xi Piluo's host of one hundred thousand collapsed in a single battle; the swarming multitudes of Henan were pacified at once.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Piluo's host of one hundred thousand collapsed in a single battle; the swarming rebels of Henan were pacified at once.

sentences.zh: 當群凶問鼎之際，黎元乏主之辰，臣第二叔翼先在幽州，總馭燕、趙，南鄰群寇，北捍旄頭，內外安撫，得免罪戾。

translations.literal: At the time when many villains were contending for the throne and the common people lacked a ruler, your servant's second uncle Yi was first at You Province, commanding Yan and Zhao; to the south he bordered the mass of rebels, to the north he held off the frontier threat; he pacified within and without and was spared guilt.
translations.idiomatic: When many villains contended for the throne and the common people lacked a ruler, your servant's second uncle Yi was at You province, commanding Yan and Zhao; to the south he bordered the mass of rebels, to the north he held the frontier; he pacified within and without and was spared guilt.

sentences.zh: 臣第五叔智建斿黑水，與王謙為鄰，式遏蠻陬，鎮綏蜀道。

translations.literal: Your servant's fifth uncle Zhi raised his banner at Heishui, bordering Wang Qian; he held back the barbarian frontier and guarded and pacified the road into Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant's fifth uncle Zhi raised his banner at Heishui, bordering Wang Qian; he held back the barbarian frontier and guarded and pacified the road into Shu.

sentences.zh: 臣兄顗作牧淮南，坐制勍敵，乘機剿定，傳首京師。

translations.literal: Your servant's elder brother Yan governed Huainan, held the fierce enemy in check, seized the moment to suppress and settle them, and sent their heads to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant's elder brother Yan governed Huainan, held the fierce enemy in check, seized the moment to suppress and settle them, and sent their heads to the capital.

sentences.zh: 王謙竊據二江，叛換三蜀。

translations.literal: Wang Qian illicitly held the Two Rivers and rebelled across the Three Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Qian illicitly held the Two Rivers and rebelled across the Three Shu.

sentences.zh: 臣第三叔義受脤廟庭，龔行天討。

translations.literal: Your servant's third uncle Yi received sacrificial meat in the ancestral temple and undertook Heaven's punitive expedition.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant's third uncle Yi received sacrificial meat in the ancestral temple and undertook Heaven's punitive expedition.

sentences.zh: 自外父叔兄弟，皆當文武重寄，或銜命危難之間，或侍衛鉤陳之側，合門誠款，冀有可明。

translations.literal: Apart from these, uncles, brothers, and cousins all bore weighty civil and military trust—some carrying orders amid peril, some guarding beside the imperial encampment; the whole house has served in sincere loyalty, and I hope this may be made clear.
translations.idiomatic: Apart from these, uncles, brothers, and cousins all bore weighty civil and military trust—some carrying orders amid peril, some guarding beside the imperial encampment; the whole house has served in sincere loyalty, and I hope this may be made clear.

sentences.zh: 伏願下泣辜之恩，降雲雨之施，追草昧之始，錄涓滴之功，則寒灰更然，枯骨生肉，不勝區區之至，謹冒死以聞。

translations.literal: I humbly wish that you would grant the favor of weeping over guilt, bestow grace like rain from the clouds, look back to the beginning in raw obscurity, and record even the smallest merit—then cold ashes would burn again and dead bones would grow flesh; unable to bear my humble utmost, I venture to risk death to report this.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly pray that you will grant the favor of weeping over guilt, bestow grace like rain from the clouds, look back to the beginning in raw obscurity, and record even the smallest merit—then cold ashes would burn again and dead bones would grow flesh; unable to bear my humble utmost, I venture to risk death to report this.

sentences.zh: 上覽表，並翼俱釋之。

translations.literal: The Emperor read the memorial and released both Yi and him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor read the memorial and released both Yi and Zhongwen.

sentences.zh: 未幾，詔仲文率兵屯白狼塞以備胡。

translations.literal: Before long he was ordered to lead troops and encamp at Bailang Pass to guard against the barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was ordered to lead troops and encamp at Bailang Pass to guard against the barbarians.

sentences.zh: 明年，拜行軍元帥，統十二總管以擊胡。

translations.literal: The next year he was appointed Campaign Marshal and commanded twelve commanders-in-chief to attack the barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was appointed campaign marshal and commanded twelve commanders-in-chief to attack the barbarians.

sentences.zh: 出服遠鎮，遇虜，破之，斬首千餘級，六畜巨萬計。

translations.literal: He went out from Fuyuan Garrison, encountered the barbarians, defeated them, took more than a thousand heads, and seized tens of thousands of livestock.
translations.idiomatic: He marched out from Fuyuan garrison, encountered the barbarians, defeated them, took more than a thousand heads, and seized tens of thousands of livestock.

sentences.zh: 於是從金河出白道，遣總管辛明瑾、元滂、賀蘭志、呂楚、段諧等二萬人出盛樂道，趨那頡山。

translations.literal: Thereupon he went out from Jinhe by the White Road, and sent the commanders Xin Mingjin, Yuan Pang, Helan Zhi, Lü Chu, Duan Xie, and others with twenty thousand men out by the Shengle Road toward Mount Naxie.
translations.idiomatic: He then marched out from Jinhe by the White Road and sent the commanders Xin Mingjin, Yuan Pang, Helan Zhi, Lü Chu, Duan Xie, and others with twenty thousand men out by the Shengle Road toward Mount Naxie.

sentences.zh: 至護軍川北，與虜相遇，可汗見仲文軍容齊肅，不戰而退。

translations.literal: When he reached north of Hujun River he encountered the barbarians; the khan saw that Zhongwen's army was arrayed in perfect order and withdrew without fighting.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached north of Hujun River he encountered the barbarians; the khan saw Zhongwen's army arrayed in perfect order and withdrew without fighting.

sentences.zh: 仲文率精騎五千，逾山追之，不及而還。

translations.literal: Zhongwen led five thousand elite cavalry, crossed the mountains in pursuit, failed to overtake them, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongwen led five thousand elite cavalry in pursuit over the mountains, failed to overtake them, and returned.

sentences.zh: 上以尚書文簿繁雜，吏多奸計，令仲文勘錄省中事。

translations.literal: The Emperor, because the documents of the Ministry of State Affairs were numerous and complex and the clerks employed many deceitful schemes, ordered Zhongwen to audit and record affairs within the ministry.
translations.idiomatic: Because the Ministry of State Affairs documents were numerous and complex and the clerks employed many deceitful schemes, the emperor ordered Zhongwen to audit and record affairs within the ministry.

sentences.zh: 其所發擿甚多，上嘉其明斷，厚加勞賞焉。

translations.literal: The cases he exposed and impeached were very many; the Emperor praised his clarity and decisiveness and richly rewarded and commended him.
translations.idiomatic: The cases he exposed were very many; the emperor praised his clarity and decisiveness and richly rewarded him.

sentences.zh: 上每憂轉運不給，仲文請決渭水，開漕渠。

translations.literal: The Emperor often worried that transport could not supply needs; Zhongwen requested that the Wei River be cut open and a canal dug.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor often worried that transport could not keep up with demand; Zhongwen requested that the Wei River be cut open and a canal dug.

sentences.zh: 上然之，使仲文總其事。

translations.literal: The Emperor approved this and had Zhongwen oversee the whole affair.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved and had Zhongwen oversee the whole affair.

sentences.zh: 及伐陳之役，拜行軍總管，以舟師自章山出漢口。

translations.literal: At the campaign against Chen he was appointed Campaign Commander-in-Chief and led the fleet out from Zhangshan to Hankou.
translations.idiomatic: During the campaign against Chen he was appointed campaign commander-in-chief and led the fleet from Zhangshan to Hankou.

sentences.zh: 陳郢州刺史荀法尚、魯山城主誕法澄、鄧沙彌等請降，秦王俊皆令仲文以兵納之。

translations.literal: Chen's Governor of Ying Province Xun Fashang, the magistrate of Lushan Dan Fachang, Deng Shami, and others requested surrender; Prince of Qin Jun ordered Zhongwen to receive them with troops.
translations.idiomatic: Chen's governor of Ying province, Xun Fashang, Lushan's magistrate Dan Fachang, Deng Shami, and others requested surrender; Prince of Qin Jun ordered Zhongwen to receive them with troops.

sentences.zh: 高智慧等作亂江南，復以行軍總管討之。

translations.literal: When Gao Zhihui and others rebelled in Jiangnan, he was again made Campaign Commander-in-Chief to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Zhihui and others rebelled in Jiangnan, he was again made campaign commander-in-chief to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 時三軍乏食，米粟踴貴，仲文私糶軍糧，坐除名。

translations.literal: At that time the three armies lacked food and grain and rice soared in price; Zhongwen privately sold army grain and was punished by removal from the register.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the three armies lacked food and grain prices soared; Zhongwen privately sold army grain and was stripped of rank and office.

sentences.zh: 明年，復官爵，率兵屯馬邑以備胡。

translations.literal: The next year his office and title were restored, and he led troops to encamp at Mayi to guard against the barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: The next year his office and title were restored, and he led troops to encamp at Mayi to guard against the barbarians.

sentences.zh: 數旬而罷。

translations.literal: After several tens of days he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: After several tens of days he was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 晉王廣以仲文有將領之才，每常屬意，至是奏之，乃令督晉王軍府事。

translations.literal: Prince of Jin Guang, because Zhongwen had the talent of a commander, had long favored him; at this time he memorialized about him, and the Emperor thereupon ordered him to oversee the affairs of the Prince of Jin's military headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Jin Guang, because Zhongwen had the talent of a commander, had long favored him; he now memorialized about him, and the emperor ordered Zhongwen to oversee the affairs of the prince's military headquarters.

sentences.zh: 後突厥犯塞，晉王為元帥，以仲文將前軍，大破賊而還。

translations.literal: Later, when the Turks raided the frontier, the Prince of Jin served as marshal; Zhongwen commanded the vanguard, greatly defeated the rebels, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when the Turks raided the frontier, Prince of Jin Guang served as marshal; Zhongwen commanded the vanguard, routed the enemy, and returned.

sentences.zh: 仁壽初，拜太子右衛率。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Renshou era he was appointed Right Commandant of the Crown Prince's Guard.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Renshou era he was appointed right commandant of the crown prince's guard.

sentences.zh: 煬帝即位，遷右翊衛大將軍，參掌文武選事。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang acceded to the throne, he was transferred to Grand General of the Right Illustrious Wing Guard and took part in managing civil and military appointments.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang acceded to the throne, he was transferred to grand general of the right illustrious wing guard and took part in managing civil and military appointments.

sentences.zh: 從帝討吐谷渾，進位光祿大夫，甚見親幸。

translations.literal: He followed the Emperor on the campaign against Tuyuhun, was promoted to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and was greatly favored.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the emperor on the campaign against Tuyuhun, was promoted to grand master of splendid happiness, and was greatly favored.

sentences.zh: 遼東之役，仲文率軍指樂浪道。

translations.literal: In the Liaodong campaign, Zhongwen led his army toward the Leyang route.
translations.idiomatic: In the Liaodong campaign, Zhongwen led his army toward the Leyang route.

sentences.zh: 軍次烏骨城，仲文簡羸馬驢數千，置於軍後。

translations.literal: The army halted at Wugu Fortress; Zhongwen selected several thousand emaciated horses and donkeys and placed them at the rear of the army.
translations.idiomatic: When the army encamped at Wugu Fortress, Zhongwen picked out several thousand scrawny horses and donkeys and posted them at the rear of the column.

sentences.zh: 既而率眾東過，高麗出兵掩襲輜重，仲文回擊，大破之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he led the host eastward in passage; Goguryeo sent troops to surprise and attack the baggage train; Zhongwen turned back to strike and greatly defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Then, as he led his forces eastward, Goguryeo troops launched a surprise raid on the baggage train; Zhongwen wheeled about to counterattack and inflicted a crushing defeat.

sentences.zh: 至鴨綠水，高麗將乙支文德詐降，來入其營。

translations.literal: When they reached the Yalu River, the Goguryeo general Eulji Mundeok feigned surrender and came into his camp.
translations.idiomatic: At the Yalu River, the Goguryeo general Eulji Mundeok pretended to surrender and entered Zhongwen's camp.

sentences.zh: 仲文先奉密旨，若遇高元及文德者，必擒之。

translations.literal: Zhongwen had earlier received a secret edict: if he encountered King Gao Yuan or Eulji Mundeok, he must seize them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongwen had previously received secret orders that if he encountered King Gao Yuan or Eulji Mundeok, he was to capture them.

sentences.zh: 至是，文德來，仲文將執之。

translations.literal: At this time Eulji Mundeok came; Zhongwen was about to seize him.
translations.idiomatic: When Eulji Mundeok arrived, Zhongwen was on the point of arresting him.

sentences.zh: 時尚書右丞劉士龍為慰撫使，固止之。

translations.literal: At the time Liu Shilong, Right Assistant Director of the Ministry of Revenue, served as pacification commissioner and firmly stopped him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shilong, right assistant director of the Ministry of Revenue, was then serving as pacification commissioner and firmly restrained him.

sentences.zh: 仲文遂舍文德。

translations.literal: Zhongwen thereupon released Eulji Mundeok.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongwen thereupon let Eulji Mundeok go.

sentences.zh: 尋悔，遣人紿文德曰：「更有言議，可複來也。

translations.literal: Soon regretting it, he sent a man to deceive Eulji Mundeok, saying: "There is more to discuss; you may come again.
translations.idiomatic: Soon regretting his decision, he sent someone to trick Eulji Mundeok, saying, "There is more to discuss—you may return.

sentences.zh: 」文德不從，遂濟。

translations.literal: " Eulji Mundeok did not comply and thereupon crossed the river.
translations.idiomatic: " Eulji Mundeok refused and crossed the river.

sentences.zh: 仲文選騎渡水追之，每戰破賊。

translations.literal: Zhongwen selected cavalry, crossed the water in pursuit, and in every battle defeated the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongwen picked cavalry, crossed the river in pursuit, and routed the enemy in battle after battle.

sentences.zh: 文德遺仲文詩曰：「神策究天文，妙算窮地理。

translations.literal: Eulji Mundeok sent Zhongwen a poem saying: "With divine stratagem probing heaven's signs, with subtle reckoning exhausting earth's features.
translations.idiomatic: Eulji Mundeok sent Zhongwen a poem that read, "Your divine stratagems plumb the heavens; your subtle calculations exhaust the earth.

sentences.zh: 戰勝功既高，知足願雲止。

translations.literal: Your battle victories merit is already high; knowing sufficiency, may your ambition cease like clouds.
translations.idiomatic: Your victories have already won you great merit; know when enough is enough, and let your ambition rest like clouds.

sentences.zh: 」仲文答書諭之，文德燒柵而遁。

translations.literal: " Zhongwen replied with a letter admonishing him; Eulji Mundeok burned his palisade and fled.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhongwen answered with a letter of admonition; Eulji Mundeok burned his stockade and fled.

sentences.zh: 時宇文述以糧盡欲還，仲文議以精銳追文德，可以有功。

translations.literal: At the time Yuwen Shu, because provisions were exhausted, wished to return; Zhongwen argued that with picked troops they should pursue Eulji Mundeok and could achieve merit.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Shu wanted to withdraw because supplies were running out, but Zhongwen argued that a pursuit with elite troops could still win glory against Eulji Mundeok.

sentences.zh: 述固止之，仲文怒曰：「將軍仗十萬之眾，不能破小賊，何顏以見帝！

translations.literal: Shu firmly stopped him; Zhongwen angrily said: "General, wielding a host of a hundred thousand, cannot crush a petty foe—what face have you to see the Emperor!
translations.idiomatic: Shu firmly objected. Zhongwen burst out, "You command a hundred thousand men and cannot break a petty band—what face will you show the emperor!

sentences.zh: 且仲文此行也，固無功矣。

translations.literal: Moreover, Zhongwen's expedition this time is indeed doomed to no achievement.
translations.idiomatic: And as for this campaign of mine—it is already doomed to failure.

sentences.zh: 」述因厲聲曰：「何以知無功？

translations.literal: " Shu thereupon said in a harsh voice: "How do you know there will be no achievement?
translations.idiomatic: " Shu snapped back, "How do you know it will fail?

sentences.zh: 」仲文曰：「昔周亞夫之為將也，見天子軍容不變。

translations.literal: " Zhongwen said: "In antiquity when Zhou Yafu served as general, he saw the Son of Heaven yet his military bearing did not change.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhongwen replied, "When Zhou Yafu commanded armies, he received the Son of Heaven yet never broke formation.

sentences.zh: 此決在一人，所以功成名遂。

translations.literal: Victory depends on one man—that is how merit is achieved and fame fulfilled.
translations.idiomatic: Victory rested on one man's will—that is how fame and success were won.

sentences.zh: 今者人各其心，何以赴敵！

translations.literal: Now each man has his own heart—how can they march against the enemy!
translations.idiomatic: Today every man follows his own mind—how can such an army face the enemy!

sentences.zh: 」初，帝以仲文有計畫，令諸軍諮稟節度，故有此言。

translations.literal: " Earlier the Emperor, because Zhongwen had plans, had ordered the armies to consult him for command—hence these words.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor had earlier entrusted Zhongwen with strategy and ordered the armies to take their direction from him—hence this remark.

sentences.zh: 由是述等不得已而從之，遂行。

translations.literal: Because of this Shu and the others had no choice but to follow him, and they set out.
translations.idiomatic: Shu and the others had no choice but to go along, and the pursuit began.

sentences.zh: 東至薩水，宇文述以兵餒退歸，師遂敗績。

translations.literal: Eastward to the Sa River, Yuwen Shu because the troops were hungry withdrew and returned; the army thereupon suffered a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: They marched east as far as the Sa River, but Yuwen Shu turned back when his men went hungry, and the army suffered a catastrophic defeat.

sentences.zh: 帝以屬吏，諸將皆委罪于仲文。

translations.literal: The Emperor handed them over to the judicial officials; all the generals shifted blame onto Zhongwen.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor handed the matter to the courts, and every general blamed Zhongwen.

sentences.zh: 帝大怒，釋諸將，獨系仲文。

translations.literal: The Emperor was greatly enraged, released the generals, and alone imprisoned Zhongwen.
translations.idiomatic: In a fury the emperor freed the other generals and imprisoned Zhongwen alone.

sentences.zh: 仲文憂恚發病，困篤方出之，卒于家，時年六十八。

translations.literal: Zhongwen, aggrieved and indignant, fell ill; only when critically ill was he released, and he died at home, aged sixty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: Grief and rage brought on illness; he was released only when near death and died at home at sixty-eight.

sentences.zh: 撰《漢書刊繁》三十卷、《略覽》三十卷。

translations.literal: He compiled Han shu kan fan in thirty scrolls and Lüe lan in thirty scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: He authored Han shu kan fan in thirty scrolls and Lüe lan in thirty scrolls.

sentences.zh: 有子九人，欽明最知名。

translations.literal: He had nine sons; Qinming was the most renowned.
translations.idiomatic: He had nine sons; Qinming was the best known.

sentences.zh: 兄顗顗字元武，身長八尺，美鬚眉。

translations.literal: His elder brother Yan—Yan, style name Yuanwu—was eight chi tall, with handsome beard and brows.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Yu Yan, style name Yuanwu, stood eight chi tall and had handsome beard and brows.

sentences.zh: 周大塚宰宇文護見而器之，妻以季女。

translations.literal: Yuwen Hu, Grand Minister of Zhou, saw him and valued him, and gave him his youngest daughter in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Hu, grand minister of Zhou, took a liking to him and married him to his youngest daughter.

sentences.zh: 尋以父勳賜爵新野郡公，邑三千戶。

translations.literal: Soon, on account of his father's merit, he was granted the title Duke of Xinye commandery, with a fief of three thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Soon, through his father's achievements, he was enfeoffed as Duke of Xinye with a fief of three thousand households.

sentences.zh: 授大都督，遷車騎大將軍、儀同三司。

translations.literal: He was appointed grand commander, then transferred to Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry and Commissioner with the Third Rank of Prestige.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed grand commander, then promoted to grand general of chariots and cavalry and commissioner with the third rank of prestige.

sentences.zh: 其後累以軍功，授上開府，曆左、右宮伯，郢州刺史。

translations.literal: Thereafter, repeatedly on account of military merit, he was appointed Senior Opener of the Way, served as left and right palace guard, and became inspector of Ying province.
translations.idiomatic: He later won repeated military honors, rose to senior opener of the way, served as left and right palace guard, and became inspector of Ying province.

sentences.zh: 大象中，以水軍總管從韋孝寬經略淮南。

translations.literal: In the Daxiang era, as commander of the water forces he followed Wei Xiaokuan in planning operations in Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: During the Daxiang reign he served as commander of the water forces under Wei Xiaokuan's Huainan campaign.

sentences.zh: 顗率開府元紹貴、上儀同毛猛等，以舟師自潁口入淮。

translations.literal: Yan led Opener of the Way Yuan Shaogui, Commissioner with the First Rank of Prestige Mao Meng, and others; with the fleet they entered the Huai from Yingkou.
translations.idiomatic: Yan led opener of the way Yuan Shaogui, commissioner with the first rank of prestige Mao Meng, and others in a fleet that entered the Huai from Yingkou.

sentences.zh: 陳防主潘深棄柵而走，進與孝寬攻拔壽陽。

translations.literal: Chen's frontier commander Pan Shen abandoned his stockade and fled; Yan advanced and with Xiaokuan captured Shouyang.
translations.idiomatic: Pan Shen, the Chen frontier commander, abandoned his stockade and fled; Yan joined Xiaokuan in capturing Shouyang.

sentences.zh: 複引師圍硤石，守將許約懼而降，顗乃拜東廣州刺史。

translations.literal: He again led the army to besiege Xiashi; the defending general Xu Yue, in fear, surrendered; Yan was thereupon appointed governor of eastern Guang province.
translations.idiomatic: He then besieged Xiashi, where the defender Xu Yue surrendered in fear, and Yan was appointed governor of Eastern Guang province.

sentences.zh: 尉迥之反也，時總管趙文表與顗素不協，顗將圖之，因臥閣內，詐得心疾，謂左右曰：「我見兩三人至我前者，輒大驚，即欲斫之，不能自製也。

translations.literal: When Yuchi Jiong rebelled, the commander Zhao Wenbiao and Yan had long been at odds; Yan intended to plot against him, and therefore lay inside his pavilion feigning heart disease, saying to those around him: "I see two or three men before me and instantly am greatly frightened; I immediately want to hack at them and cannot control myself.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuchi Jiong rebelled, Zhao Wenbiao, the area commander, had long been at odds with Yan, who now plotted against him. He lay in his chamber feigning heart trouble and told his attendants, "When two or three men appear before me I am seized with terror and want to cut them down—I cannot control myself.

sentences.zh: 」其有賓客候問者，皆令去左右。

translations.literal: " Any guest who came to inquire after him was told to leave his attendants.
translations.idiomatic: " Anyone who came to visit was made to leave his attendants behind.

sentences.zh: 顗漸稱危篤，文表往候之，令從者至大門而止，文表獨至顗所。

translations.literal: Yan gradually claimed to be critically ill; Wenbiao came to visit; he had Wenbiao's attendants stop at the great gate; Wenbiao alone reached Yan's quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Yan gradually claimed to be near death. When Wenbiao came to call, Yan had his escort halt at the gate and received Wenbiao alone.

sentences.zh: 顗醿然而起，抽刀斫殺之，」因唱言曰：「文表與尉迥通謀，所以斬之。

translations.literal: Yan suddenly sprang up, drew his sword and hacked Wenbiao to death," then proclaimed aloud: "Wenbiao conspired with Yuchi Jiong—therefore I have executed him.
translations.idiomatic: Yan suddenly leaped up, drew his sword, and cut Wenbiao down," then shouted, "Wenbiao was in league with Yuchi Jiong—that is why I killed him.

sentences.zh: 」其麾下無敢動者。

translations.literal: " None under his command dared to stir.
translations.idiomatic: " Not one man under his command dared move.

sentences.zh: 時高祖以尉迥未平，慮顗複生邊患，因而勞勉之，即拜吳州總管。
