translations.literal: At the time Emperor Gaozu, because Yuchi Jiong was not yet pacified, feared Yan might again cause border trouble; he therefore comforted and encouraged him and at once appointed him area commander of Wu province.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu, still fighting Yuchi Jiong, feared Yan might stir up trouble on the frontier; he reassured him and immediately made him area commander of Wu province.

sentences.zh: 陳將錢茂和率數千人襲江陽，顗逆擊走之。

translations.literal: The Chen general Qian Maohe led several thousand men to raid Jiangyang; Yan met the attack and drove him off.
translations.idiomatic: The Chen general Qian Maohe raided Jiangyang with several thousand men; Yan met him and drove him off.

sentences.zh: 陳複遣將陳紀、周羅睺、燕合兒等襲顗，顗拒之而退，賜彩數百段。

translations.literal: Chen again sent the generals Chen Ji, Zhou Luohou, Yan He'er, and others to attack Yan; Yan repulsed them and they withdrew; he was granted several hundred bolts of colored silk.
translations.idiomatic: Chen sent Chen Ji, Zhou Luohou, Yan He'er, and others against him; Yan beat them back and was rewarded with several hundred bolts of colored silk.

sentences.zh: 高祖受禪，文表弟詣闕稱兄無罪。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu received the abdication, Wenbiao's younger brother went to court to declare his brother innocent.
translations.idiomatic: After Gaozu took the throne, Wenbiao's younger brother petitioned the court claiming his brother had been innocent.

sentences.zh: 上令案其事，太傅竇熾等議顗當死。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered the matter investigated; Grand Tutor Dou Chi and others judged that Yan should die.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered an inquiry; Grand Tutor Dou Chi and others ruled that Yan deserved death.

sentences.zh: 上以門著勳績，特原之，貶為開府。

translations.literal: The Emperor, because the family had distinguished merit, specially pardoned him and demoted him to opener of the way.
translations.idiomatic: Because the family had served with distinction, the emperor spared him but demoted him to opener of the way.

sentences.zh: 後襲爵燕國公，邑萬六千戶。

translations.literal: Later he inherited the title Duke of Yan state, with a fief of sixteen thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: He later inherited the title Duke of Yan with a fief of sixteen thousand households.

sentences.zh: 尋以疾免。

translations.literal: Soon he was relieved on account of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon dismissed because of illness.

sentences.zh: ，拜澤州刺史。

translations.literal: , appointed governor of Ze province.
translations.idiomatic: He was then appointed governor of Ze province.

sentences.zh: 數年，免職，卒於家。

translations.literal: After several years he was dismissed from office and died at home.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later he left office and died at home.

sentences.zh: 子世虔嗣。

translations.literal: His son Shiqian succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shiqian succeeded to his rank.

sentences.zh: 從父弟璽璽字伯符。

translations.literal: His father's younger brother's son Xi—Xi, style name Bofu.
translations.idiomatic: His cousin Yu Xi, style name Bofu,

sentences.zh: 父翼，仕周為上柱國、幽州總管、任國公。

translations.literal: His father Yi served Zhou as pillar of state, area commander of You province, and Duke of Ren state.
translations.idiomatic: was the son of Yu Yi, who under Zhou had been pillar of state, area commander of You province, and Duke of Ren.

sentences.zh: 高祖為丞相，尉迥作亂，遣人誘翼。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu was chancellor, Yuchi Jiong raised rebellion and sent men to entice Yi.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu was still chancellor, Yuchi Jiong rebelled and tried to win Yi over.

sentences.zh: 翼鎖其使，送之長安，高祖甚悅。

translations.literal: Yi chained up the envoy and sent him to Chang'an; Emperor Gaozu was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Yi bound the envoy and sent him to Chang'an, greatly pleasing Gaozu.

sentences.zh: 及高祖受禪，翼入朝，上為之降榻，握手極歡。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu received the abdication, Yi entered court; the Emperor for his sake descended from the couch, clasped hands, and rejoiced exceedingly.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu took the throne, Yi came to court; the emperor stepped down from his seat, clasped his hands, and welcomed him with great warmth.

sentences.zh: 數日，拜為太尉。

translations.literal: Within several days he was appointed Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Within days he was appointed grand commandant.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，卒，諡曰穆。

translations.literal: After a little more than a year he died; his posthumous title was Mu.
translations.idiomatic: A little over a year later he died, posthumous name Mu.

sentences.zh: 璽少有器幹，仕周，起家右侍上士。

translations.literal: Xi from youth had talent and capacity; serving Zhou, he began office as right attendant upper steward.
translations.idiomatic: Xi showed ability from youth; under Zhou he entered service as right attendant upper steward.

sentences.zh: 尋授儀同，領右羽林，遷少胥附。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed commissioner with equal prestige, commanded the right feathered forest guard, and was transferred to junior adjutant of the palace guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made commissioner with equal prestige, took command of the right feathered forest guard, and became junior adjutant of the palace guard.

sentences.zh: 武帝時，從齊王憲破齊師於洛陽，以功賜爵豐寧縣子，邑五百戶。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Wu, he followed Prince of Qi Xian in defeating Qi forces at Luoyang; on account of merit he was granted the title Viscount of Fengning county, with a fief of five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Wu he followed Prince Xian of Qi in defeating Qi armies at Luoyang and was enfeoffed as viscount of Fengning with five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 尋從帝平齊，加開府，改封黎陽縣公，邑千二百戶，授職方中大夫。

translations.literal: Soon he followed the Emperor in pacifying Qi, was promoted to opener of the way, had his enfeoffment changed to Duke of Liyang county with a fief of twelve hundred households, and was appointed director of the bureau of appointments.
translations.idiomatic: He then joined the emperor in conquering Qi, rose to opener of the way, was re-enfeoffed as duke of Liyang with twelve hundred households, and was appointed director in the bureau of appointments.

sentences.zh: 及宣帝嗣位，轉右勳曹中大夫。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuan succeeded to the throne, he was transferred to right director of meritorious service.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuan came to the throne, he became right director of meritorious service.

sentences.zh: 尋領右忠義。

translations.literal: Soon he commanded the right loyal-righteous guard.
translations.idiomatic: He soon took command of the right loyal-righteous guard.

sentences.zh: 高祖為丞相，加上開府。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu was chancellor, he was promoted to senior opener of the way.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu was chancellor, he was promoted to senior opener of the way.

sentences.zh: 及受禪，進位大將軍，拜汴州刺史，甚有能名。

translations.literal: When he received the abdication, he was advanced to grand general and appointed governor of Bian province; he had a strong reputation for competence.
translations.idiomatic: At the founding of the dynasty he rose to grand general and became governor of Bian province, earning a name for capable administration.

sentences.zh: 上聞而善之，優詔褒揚，賜帛百匹。

translations.literal: The Emperor heard of it and approved; he issued a gracious edict praising him and granted a hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor heard and approved; he issued a commendatory edict and granted a hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 尋加上大將軍，進爵郡公。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to senior grand general and advanced in rank to duke of a commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to senior grand general and advanced to ducal rank.

sentences.zh: 轉邵州刺史，在州數年，甚有恩惠。

translations.literal: He was transferred to governor of Shao province; during several years in the province he showed great kindness and grace.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to governor of Shao province, he governed for years with notable kindness.

sentences.zh: 後檢校江陵總管，州人張願等數十人，詣闕上表，請留璽。

translations.literal: Later, as acting area commander of Jiangling, several dozen men of the province including Zhang Yuan went to court and submitted a memorial asking that Xi be retained.
translations.idiomatic: Later, while acting as area commander of Jiangling, several dozen local men led by Zhang Yuan petitioned the throne to keep Xi in office.

sentences.zh: 上嘉歎良久，令還邵州，父老相賀。

translations.literal: The Emperor sighed in admiration for a long time and ordered him returned to Shao province; the elders congratulated one another.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sighed in admiration and sent him back to Shao; the elders rejoiced together.

sentences.zh: 尋遷洛州刺史，複為熊州刺史，並有惠政。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to governor of Luo province, then again governor of Xiong province; in both posts he had benevolent administration.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon moved to Luo province and then Xiong province, governing both with benevolent policies.

sentences.zh: 以疾征還京師。

translations.literal: Because of illness he was summoned back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Illness brought him back to the capital.

sentences.zh: 仁壽末，卒於家，諡曰靜。

translations.literal: At the end of the Renshou era he died at home; his posthumous title was Jing.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Renshou era he died at home, posthumous name Jing.

sentences.zh: 有子志本。

translations.literal: He had a son Zhiben.
translations.idiomatic: He had a son named Zhiben.

sentences.zh: 段文振段文振，北海期原人也。

translations.literal: Duan Wenzhen—Duan Wenzhen was a native of Qiyuan in Beihai.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Wenzhen came from Qiyuan in Beihai commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖壽，魏滄州刺史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Shou was inspector of Cang province under Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Shou had been inspector of Cang province under Wei.

sentences.zh: 父威，周洮、河、甘、渭四州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Wei was inspector of the four provinces Tao, He, Gan, and Wei under Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Wei had served Zhou as inspector of Tao, He, Gan, and Wei provinces.

sentences.zh: 文振少有膂力，膽氣過人，性剛直，明達時務。

translations.literal: Wenzhen from youth had physical strength; his courage exceeded other men; his nature was upright and firm, clear and penetrating in affairs of the age.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Wenzhen was powerfully built, bolder than most, upright by nature, and shrewd in public affairs.

sentences.zh: 初為宇文護親信，護知其有幹用。

translations.literal: At first he was a trusted associate of Yuwen Hu; Hu knew he had practical ability.
translations.idiomatic: He first served as a trusted aide to Yuwen Hu, who recognized his practical talent.

sentences.zh: 擢授中外府兵曹。

translations.literal: He was promoted and appointed to the military bureau of the central and outer offices.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to the military bureau of the central and outer offices.

sentences.zh: 後武帝攻齊海昌王尉相貴于晉州，其亞將侯子欽、崔景嵩為內應。

translations.literal: Later Emperor Wu attacked Qi Prince of Haichang Wei Xianggui at Jin province; his lieutenant generals Hou Ziqin and Cui Jingsong served as inside collaborators.
translations.idiomatic: Later Emperor Wu besieged Wei's Prince of Haichang, Wei Xianggui, at Jinzhou, where lieutenant generals Hou Ziqin and Cui Jingsong acted as inside collaborators.

sentences.zh: 文振杖槊登城，與崔仲方等數十人先登。

translations.literal: Wenzhen, leaning on his spear, climbed the wall; with Cui Zhongfang and several dozen others he was among the first to ascend.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzhen scaled the wall spear in hand and was among the first up with Cui Zhongfang and several dozen others.

sentences.zh: 文振隨景嵩至相貴所，拔佩刀劫之，相貴不敢動，城遂下。

translations.literal: Wenzhen followed Jingsong to Xianggui's quarters, drew his girdle knife and seized him; Xianggui did not dare move, and the city thereupon fell.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzhen followed Jingsong to Xianggui's quarters, drew his sword, and seized him; Xianggui did not stir, and the city fell.

sentences.zh: 帝大喜，賜物千段。

translations.literal: The Emperor was greatly pleased and granted a thousand bolts of goods.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted and rewarded him with a thousand bolts of goods.

sentences.zh: 進拔文侯、華谷、高壁三城，皆有力焉。

translations.literal: He advanced to capture the three cities Wenhou, Huagu, and Gaobi—all with his strong effort.
translations.idiomatic: He went on to capture Wenhou, Huagu, and Gaobi, distinguishing himself in each.

sentences.zh: 及攻并州，陷東門而入，齊安德王延宗懼而出降。

translations.literal: When they attacked Bing province, they breached the east gate and entered; Qi Prince Ande Yan Zong, in fear, came out and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: At the assault on Bingzhou they broke in through the east gate; Prince Ande of Qi, Yan Zong, surrendered in terror.

sentences.zh: 錄前後勳，將拜高秩，以讒毀獲譴，因授上儀同，賜爵襄國縣公，邑千戶。

translations.literal: Recording his merit before and after, he was about to be appointed to high rank; because of slander by prophecy he received censure and was thereupon appointed Commissioner with the First Rank of Prestige and granted the title Duke of Xiangguo county, with a fief of a thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: His accumulated merit would have won him high rank, but prophecy slander brought censure; he received instead the first rank of prestige and was enfeoffed as duke of Xiangguo with a thousand households.

sentences.zh: 進平鄴都，又賜綺羅二千匹。

translations.literal: He advanced to pacify the capital of Ye and was again granted two thousand bolts of fine silk.
translations.idiomatic: He helped pacify the Ye capital and was again granted two thousand bolts of fine silk.

sentences.zh: 後從滕王逌擊稽胡，破之。

translations.literal: Later he followed Prince of Teng Yu in attacking the Jiahu barbarians and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: He later followed Prince Yu of Teng against the Jiahu barbarians and defeated them.

sentences.zh: 曆相州別駕、揚州總管長史。

translations.literal: He served as vice-governor of Xiang province and chief administrator under the area commander of Yang province.
translations.idiomatic: He served as vice-governor of Xiang province and chief administrator under the Yangzhou area commander.

sentences.zh: 入為天官都上士，從韋孝寬經略淮南。

translations.literal: He entered court as senior steward of the celestial bureau and followed Wei Xiaokuan in planning operations in Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: He entered court as senior steward of the celestial bureau and joined Wei Xiaokuan's Huainan campaign.

sentences.zh: 俄而尉迥作亂，時文振老母妻子俱在鄴城，迥遣人誘之，文振不顧，歸於高祖。

translations.literal: Soon Yuchi Jiong raised rebellion; at the time Wenzhen's old mother, wife, and children were all in Ye city; Jiong sent men to entice him, but Wenzhen paid no heed and returned to Emperor Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuchi Jiong rebelled, Wenzhen's mother, wife, and children were all in Ye city and Jiong tried to win him over, but he ignored the offer and returned to Gaozu.

sentences.zh: 高祖引為丞相掾，領宿衛驃騎。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu brought him in as a staff member of the chancellor and put him in command of the palace guard swift cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu took him onto the chancellor's staff and put him in charge of the palace guard swift cavalry.

sentences.zh: 司馬消難之奔陳也，高祖令文振安集淮南，還除衛尉少卿，兼內史侍郎。

translations.literal: When Sima Xiaonan fled to Chen, Emperor Gaozu ordered Wenzhen to pacify and settle Huainan; on return he was appointed Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Regalia and concurrent Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Xiaonan defected to Chen, Gaozu sent Wenzhen to pacify Huainan; on his return he became vice minister of the court of imperial regalia and concurrent vice director of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 尋以行軍長史從達奚震討叛蠻，平之，加上開府。

translations.literal: Soon, as chief administrator on campaign he followed Daxi Zhen in suppressing rebellious barbarians, pacified them, and was promoted to senior opener of the way.
translations.idiomatic: He soon served as campaign chief administrator under Daxi Zhen against rebel tribes, pacified them, and rose to senior opener of the way.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，遷鴻臚卿。

translations.literal: After a little more than a year he was transferred to Grand Master for Ceremonial Occasions.
translations.idiomatic: A little over a year later he became grand master for ceremonial occasions.

sentences.zh: 衛王爽北征突厥，以文振為長史，坐勳簿不實免官。

translations.literal: Prince Wei Shuang on the northern expedition against the Turks appointed Wenzhen chief administrator; he was dismissed from office for an inaccurate merit register.
translations.idiomatic: On Prince Shuang's northern campaign against the Turks, Wenzhen served as chief administrator but was dismissed when his merit register proved false.

sentences.zh: 後為石、河二州刺史，甚有威惠，遷蘭州總管，改封龍崗縣公。

translations.literal: Later he served as governor of Shi and He provinces; he had great authority and kindness; he was transferred to area commander of Lan province and had his enfeoffment changed to Duke of Longgang county.
translations.idiomatic: He later governed Shi and He provinces with stern fairness and kindness, became area commander of Lan province, and was re-enfeoffed as duke of Longgang.

sentences.zh: 突厥犯塞，以行軍總管擊破之，逐北至居延塞而還。

translations.literal: When the Turks raided the frontier, as campaign commander he defeated them, pursued them north to the Juyan pass, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: When Turks raided the frontier he routed them as campaign commander, pursued them to the Juyan pass, and returned.

sentences.zh: 九年，大舉伐陳，以文振為元帥秦王司馬，別領行軍總管。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, in the great campaign against Chen, Wenzhen served as staff officer to the Prince of Qin, supreme commander, and separately commanded a campaign army.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year, during the great campaign against Chen, he was staff officer to the Prince of Qin, supreme commander, and also led a campaign army of his own.

sentences.zh: 及平江南，授揚州總管司馬。

translations.literal: When Jiangnan was pacified, he was appointed chief administrator under the area commander of Yang province.
translations.idiomatic: After the pacification of Jiangnan he became chief administrator under the Yangzhou area commander.

sentences.zh: 尋轉并州總管司馬，以母憂去職。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to chief administrator under the area commander of Bing province and left office on account of mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon moved to chief administrator under the Bingzhou area commander, then left office to mourn his mother.

sentences.zh: 未幾，起令視事，固辭不許。

translations.literal: Before long he was recalled to resume duties; he firmly declined but was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he was recalled to duty; he refused firmly but was overruled.

sentences.zh: 後數年，拜雲州總管，尋為太僕卿。

translations.literal: After several years he was appointed area commander of Yun province, then Grand Master of the Court of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later he became area commander of Yun province, then grand master of the court of the imperial stud.

sentences.zh: 十九年，突厥犯塞，文振以行軍總管拒之，遇達頭可汗于沃野，擊破之。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year the Turks raided the frontier; Wenzhen as campaign commander met them and at Woye encountered Qaghan Datou and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year, when Turks raided the frontier, Wenzhen met Qaghan Datou at Woye as campaign commander and defeated him.

sentences.zh: 文振先與王世積有舊，初，文振北征，世積遺以駝馬。

translations.literal: Wenzhen had earlier been on good terms with Wang Shiji; at first, when Wenzhen marched north, Shiji sent him camels and horses.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzhen had long been friendly with Wang Shiji, who sent him camels and horses when he marched north.

sentences.zh: 比還，世積以罪被誅，文振坐與交關，功遂不錄。

translations.literal: By the time he returned, Shiji had been executed for crime; Wenzhen was punished for association with him, and his merit went unrecorded.
translations.idiomatic: By the time he returned, Shiji had been executed for treason; Wenzhen was punished for their association and his merit went unrecorded.

sentences.zh: 明年，率眾出靈州道以備胡，無虜而還。

translations.literal: The next year he led the host out by the Lingzhou route to guard against the barbarians; there were no raiders and he returned.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he led troops out the Lingzhou route to guard against barbarian raids, found none, and returned.

sentences.zh: 越巂蠻叛，文振擊平之，賜奴婢二百口。

translations.literal: The Yuexi barbarians rebelled; Wenzhen attacked and pacified them and was granted two hundred household slaves.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yuexi tribes rebelled, Wenzhen suppressed them and was granted two hundred household slaves.

sentences.zh: 仁壽初，嘉州獠作亂，文振以行軍總管討之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Renshou, the Liao of Jia province rebelled; Wenzhen as campaign commander went to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Renshou era the Jia province Liao rebelled, and Wenzhen marched against them as campaign commander.

sentences.zh: 引軍出穀間，為賊所襲，前後阻險，不得相救，軍遂大敗。

translations.literal: He led the army out through a valley pass; the bandits surprise-attacked them; front and rear were blocked by steep terrain and could not rescue one another; the army thereupon suffered a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: He led his army through a mountain defile, was ambushed, and with front and rear cut off by rough terrain could not rescue one another; the army was routed.

sentences.zh: 文振複收散兵，擊其不意，竟破之。

translations.literal: Wenzhen again gathered the scattered troops, struck where they did not expect, and in the end defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzhen rallied the scattered troops, struck where they did not expect, and in the end broke them.

sentences.zh: 文振性素剛直，無所降下，初，軍次益州，謁蜀王秀，貌頗不恭，秀甚銜之，及此，奏文振師徒喪敗。

translations.literal: Wenzhen's nature had always been upright and firm, bowing to no one; at first when the army halted at Yi province he called on Prince of Shu Xiu with a bearing quite lacking in respect; Xiu deeply resented it, and on this occasion memorialized that Wenzhen's army and followers had suffered defeat and loss.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzhen had always been proud and unyielding. When the army halted at Yi province he had visited Prince Xiu of Shu with open disrespect; Xiu bore a grudge and now reported that Wenzhen's force had been shattered.

sentences.zh: 右僕射蘇威與文振有隙，因而譖之，坐是除名。

translations.literal: Right Vice Director Su Wei had a rift with Wenzhen and therefore slandered him; on this account he was removed from the register.
translations.idiomatic: Right vice director Su Wei, who bore him a grudge, slandered him, and he was struck from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 及秀廢黜，文振上表自申理，高祖慰諭之，授大將軍。

translations.literal: When Xiu was deposed and removed, Wenzhen submitted a memorial pleading his own case; Emperor Gaozu comforted and instructed him and appointed him grand general.
translations.idiomatic: After Xiu's deposition Wenzhen petitioned in his own defense; Gaozu reassured him and restored him as grand general.

sentences.zh: 尋拜靈州總管。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed area commander of Ling province.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed area commander of Ling province.

sentences.zh: 煬帝即位，征為兵部尚書，待遇甚重。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang acceded to the throne, Wenzhen was summoned as Minister of War and treated with great weight.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang took the throne, Wenzhen was summoned as minister of war and treated with great favor.

sentences.zh: 從征吐谷渾，文振督兵屯雪山，連營三百餘裡，東接楊義臣，西連張壽，合圍渾主于覆袁川。

translations.literal: On the campaign against Tuyuhun, Wenzhen supervised troops encamped at Snow Mountain, camps linked for more than three hundred li; east he joined Yang Yichen, west he linked with Zhang Shou, jointly encircling the Tuyuhun ruler at Fuyuan River.
translations.idiomatic: On the Tuyuhun campaign Wenzhen encamped at Snow Mountain in a chain of camps more than three hundred li long, joining Yang Yichen on the east and Zhang Shou on the west to surround the Tuyuhun ruler at Fuyuan River.

sentences.zh: 以功進位右光祿大夫。

translations.literal: On account of merit he was advanced to Grand Master of Splendid Rightness.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit he was promoted to grand master of splendid rightness.

sentences.zh: 帝幸江都，以文振行江都郡事。

translations.literal: When the Emperor visited Jiangdu, Wenzhen acted in the affairs of Jiangdu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor traveled to Jiangdu, Wenzhen administered Jiangdu commandery in his stead.

sentences.zh: 文振見高祖時容納突厥啟民居於塞內，妻以公主，賞賜重疊；

translations.literal: Wenzhen saw that under Emperor Gaozu they had accepted the Turks' Qaghan Qimin residing within the frontier, given him a princess in marriage, and heaped rewards upon him;
translations.idiomatic: Wenzhen saw that under Gaozu the court had taken the Turk Qaghan Qimin inside the frontier, married him to an imperial princess, and lavished rewards on him;

sentences.zh: 及大業初，恩澤彌厚。

translations.literal: and at the beginning of Daye the grace and favor were still thicker.
translations.idiomatic: and at the start of the Daye era the favors had grown even richer.

sentences.zh: 文振以狼子野心，恐為國患，乃上表曰：「臣聞古者遠不間近，夷不亂華，周宣外攘戎狄，秦帝築城萬里，蓋遠圖良算，弗可忘也。

translations.literal: Wenzhen, because of a wolf's cub's wild heart, feared he would become a national calamity, and therefore submitted a memorial saying: "Your subject has heard that in antiquity the distant did not meddle with the near, and barbarians did not disturb the Hua; King Xuan of Zhou repelled the Rong and Di on the outside, and the First Emperor of Qin built the wall ten thousand li— all far-sighted good plans that must not be forgotten.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing the wolfish nature of the Turks, Wenzhen warned that Qimin would become a national threat and memorialized: "I have heard that in antiquity the distant did not interfere with the near and barbarians did not trouble the Hua; King Xuan of Zhou drove off the Rong and Di abroad, and the First Emperor of Qin raised walls ten thousand li—all far-sighted policies that must not be forgotten.

sentences.zh: 竊見國家容受啟民，資其兵食，假以地利。

translations.literal: Your subject has observed that the state accepts and harbors Qimin, supplies his troops and grain, and lends him strategic terrain.
translations.idiomatic: I see the state sheltering Qimin, feeding his soldiers, and granting him strategic ground.

sentences.zh: 如臣愚計，竊又未安。

translations.literal: According to your subject's foolish plan, your subject again is not at ease.
translations.idiomatic: By my humble reckoning, I cannot be at ease.

sentences.zh: 何則？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 夷狄之性，無親而貪，弱則歸投，強則反噬，蓋其本心也。

translations.literal: The nature of the Yi and Di is without kinship yet greedy; when weak they submit, when strong they turn and bite— that is their original heart.
translations.idiomatic: Barbarians know no loyalty and are ever greedy; weak, they submit; strong, they turn and bite—that is their nature.

sentences.zh: 臣學非博覽，不能遠見，且聞晉朝劉曜，梁代侯景，近事之驗，眾所共知。

translations.literal: Your subject's learning is not broad reading and cannot see far; yet I have heard of Liu Yao of the Jin dynasty and Hou Jing of the Liang, recent proofs that all together know.
translations.idiomatic: My learning is not wide and my sight not long, yet Liu Yao of Jin and Hou Jing of Liang are recent lessons everyone knows.

sentences.zh: 以臣量之，必為國患。

translations.literal: Measured by your subject, he will surely become a national calamity.
translations.idiomatic: By my measure, Qimin will surely become a national calamity.

sentences.zh: 如臣之計，以時喻遣，令出塞外。

translations.literal: According to your subject's plan, in timely fashion instruct and send him away, ordering him out beyond the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: My counsel is to instruct him in good time and send him beyond the frontier.

sentences.zh: 然後明設烽候，緣邊鎮防，務令嚴重，此乃萬歲之長策也。

translations.literal: Then clearly establish beacon fires and garrison the border with strict weight— this is the long plan for ten thousand years.
translations.idiomatic: Then set beacons clearly, fortify the border strictly, and hold the line—that is the policy for ages to come.

sentences.zh: 」時兵曹郎斛斯政專掌兵事，文振知政險薄，不可委以機要，屢言於帝，帝並弗納。

translations.literal: " At the time Military Affairs Officer Husizheng alone managed military affairs; Wenzhen knew Zheng was dangerous and shallow and could not be entrusted with crucial matters; he repeatedly spoke to the Emperor, and the Emperor altogether did not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: " At the time Husizheng, officer of military affairs, controlled the armies alone. Wenzhen saw that he was treacherous and shallow and unfit for secrets; he warned the emperor again and again, but the emperor would not listen.

sentences.zh: 及遼東之役，授左候衛大將軍，出南蘇道。

translations.literal: When the Liaodong campaign came, he was appointed Grand General of the Left Guard and marched out by the Nansu route.
translations.idiomatic: When the Liaodong campaign began, he was appointed grand general of the left guard and marched by the Nansu route.

sentences.zh: 在道疾篤，上表曰：「臣以庸微，幸逢聖世，濫蒙獎擢，榮冠儕伍。

translations.literal: On the march his illness grew critical; he submitted a memorial saying: "Your subject, being mediocre and slight, has fortunately met a sage age, recklessly received promotion and selection, and my honor tops my peers.
translations.idiomatic: On the march his illness turned grave; he memorialized: "I am a man of little worth who has been favored in a sage reign, promoted beyond my desert, and honored above my peers.

sentences.zh: 而智能無取，叨竊已多，言念國恩，用忘寢食。

translations.literal: Yet my ability and wisdom have nothing to take; I have presumptuously stolen too much; thinking on the state's grace, I forget sleep and food.
translations.idiomatic: Yet I have no talent to show for it and have taken more than I deserve; remembering the state's kindness, I forget sleep and food.

sentences.zh: 常思效其鳴吠，以報萬分，而攝養乖方，疾患遂篤。

translations.literal: I always think to repay with a dog's bark a ten-thousandth part, yet my regimen was wrong and my illness has become critical.
translations.idiomatic: I have always hoped to repay even a fraction of my debt, but bad care has brought me to death's door.

sentences.zh: 抱此深愧，永歸泉壤，不勝餘恨，輕陳管穴。

translations.literal: Bearing this deep shame, I shall forever return to the springs; unable to overcome remaining regret, I lightly offer a narrow view.
translations.idiomatic: I go to the grave ashamed, yet cannot silence one last counsel.

sentences.zh: 竊見遼東小丑，未服嚴刑，遠降六師，親勞萬乘。

translations.literal: Your subject has observed that the petty foe of Liaodong has not yet submitted to stern punishment; from afar you have lowered six armies and personally toiled the imperial chariot.
translations.idiomatic: The petty kingdom of Liaodong still defies your majesty's wrath, yet six armies have marched from afar and the Son of Heaven himself has taken the field.

sentences.zh: 但夷狄多詐，深須防擬，口陳降款，心懷背叛，詭伏多端，勿得便受。

translations.literal: But the Yi and Di are much given to deception; one must deeply guard against them; they declare surrender with the mouth yet harbor betrayal in the heart, hiding and lying in many ways— do not readily accept them.
translations.idiomatic: Barbarians are full of deceit and must be watched closely: they offer surrender with their lips while plotting treachery in their hearts—do not trust them lightly.

sentences.zh: 水潦方降，不可淹遲，唯願嚴勒諸軍，星馳速發，水陸俱前，出其不意，則平壤孤城，勢可拔也。

translations.literal: Floodwaters are about to rise; one must not delay; I only wish you strictly to drive the armies, galloping like stars in haste to set out; land and water advance together, taking them unawares— then the isolated fortress of Pyongyang can by its momentum be taken.
translations.idiomatic: The rains are coming and there must be no delay: drive every army forward at once by land and water, strike before they expect it, and isolated Pyongyang can fall.

sentences.zh: 若傾其本根，餘城自克。

translations.literal: If you overturn their root trunk, the remaining cities will submit of themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Uproot their capital and the outlying cities will fall of themselves.

sentences.zh: 如不時定，脫遇秋霖，深為艱阻，兵糧又竭，強敵在前，靺軻出後，遲疑不決，非上策也。

translations.literal: If you do not settle them in timely fashion, should you chance upon autumn rains the hardship and obstruction will be deep; army grain will again be exhausted; a strong foe will be before you and the Mohe will emerge behind; hesitation and indecision is not the upper plan.
translations.idiomatic: If you hesitate, autumn rains will bog the armies, supplies will fail, Goguryeo will stand before you and the Mohe will strike from behind—delay is the worst strategy.

sentences.zh: 」後數日，卒于師。

translations.literal: " Several days later he died in the army.
translations.idiomatic: " A few days later he died on campaign.

sentences.zh: 帝省表，悲歎久之，贈光祿大夫、尚書右僕射、北平侯，諡曰襄。

translations.literal: The Emperor read the memorial, sighed in grief for a long time, and posthumously granted Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Right Vice Director, and Marquis of Beiping; his posthumous title was Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor read the memorial and mourned at length, posthumously granting him grand master of splendid happiness, right vice director, and the marquisate of Beiping, posthumous name Xiang.

sentences.zh: 賜物一千段，粟麥二千石，威儀鼓吹，送至墓所。

translations.literal: He granted a thousand bolts of goods, two thousand shi of millet and wheat, regalia and martial music, and sent them to the grave site.
translations.idiomatic: He granted a thousand bolts of goods, two thousand shi of grain, full funeral honors, and an escort to the tomb.

sentences.zh: 有子十人。

translations.literal: He had ten sons.
translations.idiomatic: He had ten sons.

sentences.zh: 長子詮，官至武牙郎將。

translations.literal: The eldest son Quan reached the office of General of the Martial Tooth Guard.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Quan rose to general of the martial tooth guard.

sentences.zh: 次綸，少以俠氣聞。

translations.literal: The second Lun from youth was known for chivalrous spirit.
translations.idiomatic: The second son, Lun, was known from youth for his chivalrous spirit.

sentences.zh: 文振弟文操，大業中，為武賁郎將，性甚剛嚴。

translations.literal: Wenzhen's younger brother Wencao, in the Daye era, was General of the Martial Tiger Guard; his nature was very stern and severe.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzhen's younger brother Wencao, a martial tiger guard general in the Daye era, was notoriously harsh.

sentences.zh: 帝令督秘書省學士。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered him to supervise the scholars of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor put him in charge of the secretariat scholars.

sentences.zh: 時學士頗存儒雅，文操輒鞭撻之，前後或至千數，時議者鄙之。

translations.literal: At the time the scholars largely preserved refined elegance; Wencao would always flog them; before and after it sometimes reached a thousand; those who commented at the time despised him for it.
translations.idiomatic: The scholars were men of refinement, yet Wencao flogged them relentlessly—sometimes a thousand lashes in all—and public opinion scorned him.

sentences.zh: 【論】史臣曰：仲方兼資文武，雅有籌算，伐陳之策，信為深遠矣。

translations.literal: 【論】The historiographer says: Zhongfang combined civil and military talent and had elegant plans and reckoning; his strategy for attacking Chen was truly far-reaching.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: The historiographer writes: Zhongfang united civil and military gifts and possessed elegant strategy; his plan to attack Chen was truly far-sighted.

sentences.zh: 聲績克舉，夫豈徒言哉！

translations.literal: His reputation and achievement were fully realized— was it empty talk alone!
translations.idiomatic: His fame and achievement were fully realized—this was no empty boast.

sentences.zh: 仲文博涉書記，以英略自許，尉迥之亂，遂立功名。

translations.literal: Zhongwen was broadly versed in books and records and prided himself on heroic strategy; in the chaos of Yuchi Jiong he thereupon established merit and fame.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongwen was widely read and counted himself a strategist; in Yuchi Jiong's rebellion he won his place in history.

sentences.zh: 自茲厥後，屢當推轂。

translations.literal: From this time onward he repeatedly bore the commander's chariot pole.
translations.idiomatic: From then on he repeatedly held supreme command.

sentences.zh: 遼東之役，實喪師徒。

translations.literal: In the Liaodong campaign he truly lost army and followers.
translations.idiomatic: The Liaodong campaign truly cost him his army.

sentences.zh: 斯乃大樹將顛，蓋亦非戰人之罪也。

translations.literal: This was the great tree about to topple— it was also not the fault of the fighting man alone.
translations.idiomatic: The great tree was already falling—it was not the warrior's fault alone.

sentences.zh: 文振少以膽略見重，終懷壯夫之志，時進讜言，頻稱諒直。

translations.literal: Wenzhen from youth was valued for courage and strategy; to the end he cherished the strong man's will; he timely offered forthright words and was repeatedly praised for honest bluntness.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzhen was honored from youth for courage and counsel; to the end he kept a soldier's heart, spoke plainly when it mattered, and was repeatedly praised for blunt honesty.

sentences.zh: 其取高位厚秩，良有以也。

translations.literal: That he obtained high rank and thick salary— truly he had reason for it.
translations.idiomatic: That he rose to high rank and rich reward was well deserved.
